title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘
title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘 Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan

sentences.zh: 向雄 段灼 閻纘

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan.

sentences.zh: 向雄，字茂伯，河內山陽人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong, courtesy name Maobo, was a native of Shanyang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong, courtesy name Maobo, came from Shanyang in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父韶，彭城太守。

translations.literal: Father Shao was Governor of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang Shao had governed Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 雄初仕郡為主簿，事太守王經。

translations.literal: Xiong first served the commandery as chief clerk, attending Governor Wang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as the commandery chief clerk under Governor Wang Jing.

sentences.zh: 及經之死也，雄哭之盡哀，市人咸為之悲。

translations.literal: When Jing died, Xiong wept for him with utmost grief; market folk all sorrowed for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jing was executed, Xiang Xiong mourned him openly until every onlooker in the market wept.

sentences.zh: 後太守劉毅嘗以非罪笞雄，及吳奮代毅為太守，又以少譴系雄於獄。

translations.literal: Later Governor Liu Yi once flogged Xiong without real crime; when Wu Fen replaced Yi as governor, again over a slight fault chained Xiong in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Liu Yi had him flogged on a trumped-up charge; when Wu Fen succeeded Liu, he jailed Xiang Xiong again over a petty slight.

sentences.zh: 司隸鐘會於獄中辟雄為都官從事，會死無人殯斂，雄迎喪而葬之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Zhong Hui in prison summoned Xiong as clerk for capital affairs; when Hui died none arranged burial—Xiong welcomed the coffin and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Zhong Hui pulled him from jail as capital clerk; after Zhong Hui died unmourned, Xiang Xiong claimed the body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 文帝召雄而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭王經於東市，我不問也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned Xiong and reproached him: "Formerly when Wang Jing died, you wept for Wang Jing at the eastern market—I did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen called him in: "You openly mourned Wang Jing at the eastern market—I let it pass.

sentences.zh: 今鐘會躬為叛逆，又輒收葬，若復相容，其如王法何！

translations.literal: Now Zhong Hui personally was a rebel—yet you again collected and buried him—if again tolerated—what of royal law!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was a traitor, yet you buried him too—keep indulging you and what becomes of the law?"

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「昔者先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後葬之哉！

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Formerly the former kings covered bones and buried corpses—kindness flowed to rotten bones—at the time did they first divine merit and crime before burying!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong replied: "Ancient kings gathered the fallen dead—mercy reached whitening bones—did they weigh guilt before digging graves?

sentences.zh: 今王誅既加，於法已備。

translations.literal: Now royal punishment has already been applied—to law already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial justice has already struck; the statute is satisfied.

sentences.zh: 雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。

translations.literal: Xiong moved by duty collected burial—instruction also without deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: I buried him from duty; moral teaching loses nothing by it.

sentences.zh: 法立於上，教弘於下，何必使雄違生背死以立于時！

translations.literal: Law stands above; instruction spreads below—why must Xiong oppose life and betray death to stand in the age!
translations.idiomatic: Law rules from above; morals spread below—why force me to choose between the living and the dead?

sentences.zh: 殿下仇枯骨而捐之中野，為將來仁賢之資，不亦惜乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness hates dry bones and casts them in the wild—making capital for later benevolent worthies—is this not regrettable!"
translations.idiomatic: Would you leave bones for scavengers and teach posterity that decency is wasted effort?"

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅，與談宴而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly delighted—talked feast with him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Sima Zhao feasted him and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted step by step to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時吳奮、劉毅俱為侍中，同在門下，雄初不交言。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Fen and Liu Yi both were Palace Attendants—together under the gate—Xiong at first exchanged no words.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen and Liu Yi both served as Palace Attendants alongside him—he refused to speak to either.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，敕雄令復君臣之好。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard it—ordered Xiong to restore ruler-minister goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered him to mend fences with his old superiors.

sentences.zh: 雄不得已，乃詣毅，再拜曰：「向被詔命，君臣義絕，如何？

translations.literal: Xiong having no choice—went to Yi—twice bowed saying: "Recently receiving edict command—ruler-minister righteousness cut off—how?"
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, he visited Liu Yi, bowed twice, and said, "The edict tells me to pretend we are friends—how can I?"

sentences.zh: 」於是即去。

translations.literal: Thereupon immediately departed.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on his heel and left.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大怒，問雄曰：「我令卿復君臣之好，何以故絕？

translations.literal: The emperor hearing greatly angry—asked Xiong: "I ordered you to restore ruler-minister goodwill—why intentionally cut off?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thundered, "I told you to reconcile—why did you walk out?"

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「古之君子進人以禮，退人以禮；

translations.literal: Xiong said: "The gentlemen of antiquity advanced people by ritual—dismissed people by ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong said, "Ancient worthies advanced and dismissed men through ritual;

sentences.zh: 今之進人若加諸膝，退人若墜諸川。

translations.literal: Today's advancing people is like placing them on the knee—dismissing people like dropping them into the river.
translations.idiomatic: today favorites ride on your lap; the dismissed land in the abyss.

sentences.zh: 劉河內於臣不為戎首，亦已幸甚，安復為君臣之好！

translations.literal: Liu Henei toward your servant did not become war-leader—already extremely fortunate—how again restore ruler-minister goodwill!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi stopped short of assassinating me—that is mercy enough—how can we play at cordiality?"

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let it drop.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，累遷秦州刺史，假赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In Taishi era—promoted step by step to Inspector of Qin Province—borrowed crimson canopy, curved parasol, drum and flute—gifted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi he rose to Inspector of Qin with crimson banner, curved shade, military band, and two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，入為御史中丞，遷侍中，又出為征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At Xianning beginning—entered as Palace Assistant Clerk—promoted Palace Attendant—again went out as General Who Subdues Captives.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he became Palace Assistant Clerk, then Palace Attendant, then General Who Subdues Captives in the field.

sentences.zh: 太康初，為河南尹，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: At Taikang beginning—became Governor of Henan—enfeoffed Secondary Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he governed Henan as a passes marquis.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將歸籓，雄諫曰：「陛下子弟雖多，然有名望者少。

translations.literal: Prince Qi You was about to return to his fief—Xiong remonstrated: "Your Majesty's sons and younger brothers though many—yet those with fame and repute are few.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You prepared to leave for his princedom, Xiang Xiong warned, "Your sons are numerous but few enjoy real prestige.

sentences.zh: 齊王臥在京邑，所益實深，不可不思。

translations.literal: Prince Qi lying in the capital—what it benefits is truly deep—cannot fail to ponder.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping Prince You in the capital pays enormous dividends—you must think twice.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 雄固諫忤旨，起而徑出，遂以憤卒。

translations.literal: Xiong firmly remonstrated offending intent—rose and went straight out—thereupon died of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong pressed until the emperor snapped; he stormed out and died of rage.

sentences.zh: 弟匡，惠帝世為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kuang—in Emperor Hui's age was General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xiang Kuang served Emperor Hui as General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 段灼，字休然，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Duan Zhuo, courtesy name Xiuran, was a native of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo, courtesy name Xiuran, hailed from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為西土著姓，果直有才辯。

translations.literal: For generations a great surname of the western lands—frank and upright with talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was an old Dunhuang house—blunt, talented, and silver-tongued.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，稍遷鄧艾鎮西司馬，從艾破蜀有功，封關內侯，累遷議郎。

translations.literal: Youth served province and commandery—gradually promoted Deng Ai Army Adjutant on the west—followed Ai in crushing Shu with merit—enfeoffed Secondary Marquis within the Passes—promoted step by step to Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through local posts to Deng Ai's western army adjutant, earned a passes marquisate in the Shu campaign, and climbed to Consultant.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，灼上疏追理艾曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Zhuo submitted memorial pursuing judgment for Ai:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Duan Zhuo memorialized to clear Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 故征西將軍鄧艾，心懷至忠，而荷反逆之名；

translations.literal: Former General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai—heart embracing utmost loyalty—yet bore the name of rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: General Deng Ai was utterly loyal yet branded a traitor;

sentences.zh: 平定巴、蜀，而受三族之誅，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: pacified Ba and Shu—yet received execution of three clans—your servant privately mourns him.
translations.idiomatic: he conquered Ba-Shu yet his three clans were extirpated—I grieve for him.

sentences.zh: 惜哉，言艾之反也！

translations.literal: Alas, speaking of Ai's rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: They called it rebellion—what a lie!

sentences.zh: 以艾性剛急，矜功伐善，而不能協同朋類，輕犯雅俗，失君子之心，故莫肯理之。

translations.literal: Because Ai's nature was harsh and impatient—boasted merit and praised himself—yet could not cooperate with peers—lightly offended refined custom—lost gentlemen's hearts—therefore none willing to judge for him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai was brusque and vain, rubbed peers wrong, offended polite society—so nobody defended him.

sentences.zh: 臣敢昧死言艾所以不反之狀。

translations.literal: Your servant dares risk death stating Ai's appearance of not rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: I risk my neck to show why Deng Ai never meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 艾本屯田掌犢人，宣皇帝拔之于農吏之中，顯之於宰府之職。

translations.literal: Ai originally was colonization officer tending calves—Emperor Xuan pulled him from among farming clerks—displayed him in ministerial office duties.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai began as a pasture clerk; Emperor Xuan pulled him from the fields into high office.

sentences.zh: 處內外之官，據文武之任，所在輒有名績，固足以明宣皇帝之知人矣。

translations.literal: Occupying inner and outer offices—holding civil and military charges—wherever posted immediately had famed accomplishment—solidly sufficient to clarify Emperor Xuan's knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: In civil and military posts he scored triumph after triumph—proof that Emperor Xuan could judge talent.

sentences.zh: 會值洮西之役，官兵失利，刺史王經困於圍城之中。

translations.literal: Encountering the Tao west campaign—government troops suffered defeat—Inspector Wang Jing was trapped inside besieged walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tao river campaign collapsed, Inspector Wang Jing was trapped in siege.

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，二州危懼，隴右懍懍，幾非國家之有也。

translations.literal: At that time two provinces feared peril—Longyou trembled—almost was not the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces panicked; Longyou shook—the northwest nearly slipped away.

sentences.zh: 先帝以為深憂重慮，思惟可以安邊殺敵莫賢于艾，故授之以兵馬，解狄道之圍。

translations.literal: The late emperor considered it deep worry heavy thought—thinking who could settle borders kill enemies none worthier than Ai—therefore entrusted him with troops and horses—relieved Di dao's siege.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor knew only Deng Ai could save the frontier—he gave him troops and lifted the siege at Didao.

sentences.zh: 圍解，留屯上邽。

translations.literal: Siege relieved—remained garrisoned at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After the relief he camped at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 承官軍大敗之後，士卒破膽，將吏無氣，倉庫空虛，器械殫盡。

translations.literal: Receiving after government troops great defeat—soldiers broken courage—commanders and clerks without breath—granaries empty—implements exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After that rout morale shattered, arsenals emptied, stores vanished.

sentences.zh: 艾欲積穀強兵，以待有事。

translations.literal: Ai wished to accumulate grain strengthen troops—to await events.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai meant to rebuild grain and troops against whatever came next.

sentences.zh: 是歲少雨，又為區種之法，手執耒耜，率先將士，所統萬數，而身不離僕虜之勞，親執士卒之役。

translations.literal: This year had little rain—again used field-plot methods—hand holding plow and spade—took lead before generals and soldiers—those under command ten thousand in number—yet body did not leave labor of servants and captives—personally performed soldiers' toil.
translations.idiomatic: Rain failed that year, so he tilled in grid-plots, hoe in hand, outworking his men—ten thousand under his command, yet he sweated like a conscript.

sentences.zh: 故落門、段谷之戰，能以少擊多，摧破強賊，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: Therefore in Luomen and Dangu battles—able with few strike many—smashed strong bandits—severed heads counted in myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at Luomen and Dangu he routed superior forces and piled tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 遂委艾以廟勝成圖，指授長策。

translations.literal: Thereupon entrusted Ai with temple-victory completed plans—pointed instruction long strategies.
translations.idiomatic: The court handed him the blueprint for final victory.

sentences.zh: 艾受命忘身，龍驤麟振，前無堅敵。

translations.literal: Ai receiving mandate forgot body—dragon soaring unicorn shaking—before him no firm enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed orders without sparing himself—charging like dragon or kirin—nothing stood firm before him.

sentences.zh: 蜀地阻險，山高穀深，而艾步乘不滿二萬，束馬懸車，自投死地，勇氣陵雲，將士乘勢，故能使劉禪震怖，君臣面縛。

translations.literal: Shu terrain blocked perilous—mountains high valleys deep—yet Ai's infantry and cavalry not full twenty thousand—tied horses suspended carts—threw self into dead ground—courage climbed clouds—generals and soldiers rode momentum—therefore able to make Liu Shan tremble in fear—ruler and ministers bound face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was sheer cliffs and deep defiles; Deng Ai led fewer than twenty thousand foot and horse, hoisted carts up cliffs, marched into death ground—courage pierced the clouds—until Liu Shan surrendered himself.

sentences.zh: 軍不逾時，而巴、蜀蕩定，此艾固足以彰先帝之善任矣。

translations.literal: Army not exceeding season—and Ba and Shu swept pacified—this Ai solidly sufficient to manifest the late emperor's good employment.
translations.idiomatic: In mere months Ba-Shu fell—a testament to the late emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 艾功名已成，亦當書之竹帛，傳祚萬世。

translations.literal: Ai's merit and fame already completed—also ought be written on bamboo and silk—transmit blessing myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: His fame deserved bamboo slips and silk—for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 七十老公，復何所求哉！

translations.literal: Seventy-year-old old man—again what seeking!
translations.idiomatic: A man of seventy—what more could he want?

sentences.zh: 艾以禪初降，遠郡未附，矯令承制，權安社稷。

translations.literal: Ai because Shan first surrendered—distant commanderies not yet attached—falsified orders acting on mandate—temporarily stabilizing altars and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan had just yielded and outlying districts wavered—Deng Ai issued emergency orders to steady the state.

sentences.zh: 雖違常科，有合古義，原心定罪，事可詳論。

translations.literal: Though violated standing statutes—had accord with ancient righteousness—trace heart fix crime—affairs permit detailed discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He bent regulations on purpose—yet matched classical precedent—judge his intent, not just the letter.

sentences.zh: 故鎮西將軍鐘會，有吞天下之心，恐艾威名，知必不同，因其疑似，構成其事。

translations.literal: Therefore General Who Subdues the West Zhong Hui—had heart swallowing All under Heaven—feared Ai's awe-striking name—knew surely would not agree—thereby using his suspicious likeness—constructed his affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui meant to seize the realm; he feared Deng Ai's prestige and framed him on suspicion.

sentences.zh: 艾被詔書，即遣強兵，束身就縛，不敢顧望。

translations.literal: Ai receiving edict script—immediately dispatched strong troops—bound body accepting bonds—did not dare look back.
translations.idiomatic: When the summons arrived Deng Ai sent escort troops and submitted to bonds—never hesitating.

sentences.zh: 誠自知奉見先帝，必無當死之理也。

translations.literal: Truly self-knowing audience with late emperor—certainly without ought-die principle.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted that facing the late emperor he could clear himself.

sentences.zh: 會受誅之後，艾參佐官屬、部曲將吏，愚戇相聚，自共追艾，破壞檻車，解其囚執。

translations.literal: After Hui received execution—Ai's adjutant officials, division commanders and clerks—foolish thick gathered together—themselves together pursued Ai—broke prison cart—released his prisoner bonds.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui died, Deng Ai's staff mobbed together, smashed his cage, and freed him.

sentences.zh: 艾在困地，是以狼狽失據。

translations.literal: Ai in trapped ground—therefore flustered lost footing.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered and desperate, he stumbled.

sentences.zh: 夫反非小事，若懷噁心，即當謀及豪傑，然後乃能興動大眾，不聞艾有腹心一人。

translations.literal: Rebellion is not small matter—if harboring evil heart—then ought plot reaching heroes—afterward then able to stir moving great masses—never heard Ai had one confidant in belly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion takes planning—yet Deng Ai had no inner circle.

sentences.zh: 臨死口無惡言，獨受腹背之誅，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Facing death mouth had no evil words—alone received belly-back execution—is this not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: He died without a bitter word—executed front and back—can anyone not weep?

sentences.zh: 故見之者垂涕，聞之者歎息。

translations.literal: Therefore those who saw shed tears—those who heard sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses wept; listeners groaned.

sentences.zh: 此賈誼所以慷慨于漢文，天下之事可為痛哭者，良有以也。

translations.literal: This is why Jia Yi therefore generous toward Emperor Wen of Han—All under Heaven's affairs may be things worth bitter crying—indeed there is cause.
translations.idiomatic: This is Jia Yi's grief for Emperor Wen—cause for the realm to wail.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，闡弘大度，受誅之家，不拘敘用，聽艾立後，祭祀不絕。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dragon rising—expanding great tolerance—families receiving execution—not bound by narrative employment—heard Ai establish heir—sacrifice not cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Your dragon ascent brought mercy—even struck families find posts; Deng Ai's heir may yet inherit offerings.

sentences.zh: 昔秦人憐白起之無罪，吳人傷子胥之冤酷，皆為之立祠。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin people pitied Bai Qi's without crime—Wu people wounded Zixu's cruel injustice—all for them established shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Qin mourned Bai Qi; Wu mourned Wu Zixiu—the world raised shrines.

sentences.zh: 天下之人為艾悼心痛恨，亦由是也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven's people for Ai mourn heart bitter hate—also from this.
translations.idiomatic: The empire aches for Deng Ai for the same reasons.

sentences.zh: 謂可聽艾門生故吏收艾屍柩，歸葬舊墓，還其田宅，以平蜀之功，繼封其後，使艾闔棺定諡，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it permissible to hear Ai's disciples and former clerks collect Ai's coffin—return bury old tomb—return his fields and houses—by pacifying Shu's merit—continue enfeoff his posterity—cause Ai close coffin fix posthumous title—death without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Let his old aides recover his body, bury him at home, restore his lands, enfeoff his heirs for the Shu conquest—give him a verdict and peace in the grave.

sentences.zh: 赦冤魂于黃泉，收信義於後世，則天下徇名之士，思立功之臣，必投湯火，樂為陛下死矣！

translations.literal: Pardon wronged souls in yellow springs—gather trust and righteousness in later generations—then All under Heaven's fame-seeking gentlemen—thought merit-establishing ministers—surely will cast into boiling fire—gladly die for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Right the ghost in Hades, teach posterity good faith, and every ambitious hero will leap through fire for you!

sentences.zh: 帝省表，甚嘉其意。

translations.literal: The emperor examined memorial—greatly praised its intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and praised his intent.

sentences.zh: 灼後復陳時宜曰：

translations.literal: Zhuo afterward again presented timely affairs:
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo later laid out policy again:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard heaven's seasons are not as good as earth's advantages—earth's advantages are not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's timing, earth's terrain, and human unity—Mencius ranked them just so.

sentences.zh: 三里之城，五里之郭，圜圍而攻之，有不克者，此天時不如地利。

translations.literal: Walled town three li—outer wall five li—surround attack it—there are cases not conquering—this heaven's seasons not as good as earth's advantages.
translations.idiomatic: Surround a tiny fortress yet fail—timing loses to terrain.

sentences.zh: 城非不高，池非不深，穀非不多，兵非不利，委而去之，此地利不如人和。

translations.literal: Wall not not high—moat not not deep—grain not not much—troops not not sharp—yet abandon and leave it—this earth's advantages not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Strong walls and deep moats fall when the people turn away.

sentences.zh: 然古之王者，非不先推恩德，結固人心。

translations.literal: Yet ancient kings—not without first extending grace virtue—binding firm human hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings won hearts before ramparts.

sentences.zh: 人心苟和，雖三里之城，五里之郭，不可攻也。

translations.literal: Human hearts if harmonious—though walled town three li—outer wall five li—cannot attack.
translations.idiomatic: United hearts make even a hamlet untakable.

sentences.zh: 人心不和，雖金城湯池，不能守也。

translations.literal: Human hearts if not harmonious—though metal city boiling moat—cannot defend.
translations.idiomatic: Divided hearts doom metal walls and boiling moats.

sentences.zh: 臣推此以廣其義，舜彈五弦之琴，詠《南風》之詩，而天下自理，由堯人可比屋而封也。

translations.literal: Your servant extends this to broaden its meaning—Shun plucked five-string zither—chanted South Wind ode—and All under Heaven self-ordered—because Yao's people could house-to-house enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: Shun sang "South Wind" and order followed—Yao's subjects were fit for neighborly rule.

sentences.zh: 曩者多難，奸雄屢起，攪亂眾心，刀鋸相乘，流死之孤，哀聲未絕。

translations.literal: Formerly many hardships—treacherous heroes repeatedly arose—stirring chaotic multitude hearts—knife and saw multiplied—flowing death's orphans—mourning sound not ended.
translations.idiomatic: Years of warlords shredded loyalty; blade on blade left orphans still keening.

sentences.zh: 故臣以為陛下當深思遠念，杜漸防萌，彈琴詠詩，垂拱而已。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant considers Your Majesty ought deeply ponder far thought—stop gradual prevent sprouts—pluck zither chant poems—hang draped sleeves and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Think deep, nip plots early—rule like Shun with lyre and ode alone.

sentences.zh: 其要莫若推恩以協和黎庶，故推恩足以保四海，不推恩不足以保妻子。

translations.literal: Its essence none like extending grace to harmonize black-headed populace—therefore extending grace sufficient to preserve four seas—not extending grace not sufficient to preserve wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing matters like kindness to the people—kindness secures the realm; its absence imperils your family.

sentences.zh: 是故唐堯以親睦九族為先，周文以刑于寡妻為急，明王聖主莫不先親後疏，自近及遠。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang Yao took intimate harmony nine clans first—Zhou Wen took patterning scant wife urgent—enlightened kings sagely lords none not first kin afterward distant—from near reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Yao harmonized nine kin; Wen instructed his consort first—every sage honored family before strangers.

sentences.zh: 臣以為太宰、司徒、衛將軍三王宜留洛中鎮守，其餘諸王自州征足任者，年十五以上悉遣之國。

translations.literal: Your servant considers Grand Mentor, Minister of Education, General Who Guards three kings ought remain in Luoyang guarding—the rest of various kings from province recruitment adequate candidates—age fifteen above all dispatch them to states.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the Grand Mentor, Minister of Education, and Guards general in Luoyang; send every other prince older than fifteen to his fief.

sentences.zh: 為選中郎傅相，才兼文武，以輔佐之。

translations.literal: For them select Palace Gentleman instructors and tutors—talent spanning civil and military—to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Give each prince tutors both civil and martial.

sentences.zh: 聽于其國繕修兵馬，廣布恩信。

translations.literal: Permit in their states repair weapons horses—broadly spread grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Let them drill troops and earn loyalty at home.

sentences.zh: 必撫下猶子，愛國如家，君臣分定，百世不遷，連城開地，為晉、魯、衛。

translations.literal: Surely soothe subordinates like nephews—love state like family—ruler-minister portions fixed—hundred generations not shifting—linked walls opening lands—become Jin, Lu, Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They will treat subjects as nephews and realms as households—fixed roles for generations—strong as Jin, Lu, or Wei.

sentences.zh: 所謂磐石之宗，天下服其強矣。

translations.literal: So-called granite clan—All under Heaven submits to their strength.
translations.idiomatic: That is how you forge bedrock kin and awe the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖云割地，譬猶囊漏貯中，亦一家之有耳。

translations.literal: Though saying carving lands—it compares also to leaking pouch storing inside—also one family's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting domains only moves revenue within the imperial purse.

sentences.zh: 若慮後世強大，自可豫為制度，使得推恩以分子弟。

translations.literal: If worrying later generations strong large—self may beforehand establish institutions—cause able extend grace dividing sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Fear strong cadet lines? Lay laws now for junior splits.

sentences.zh: 如此則枝分葉布，稍自削小，漸使轉至萬國，亦後世之利，非所患也。

translations.literal: Like this then branches divide leaves spread—gradually self shrink small—gradually cause shift reaching myriad states—also later generation's advantage—not what is worried.
translations.idiomatic: Branches thin over time until myriad manageable states—posterity gains, not grief.

sentences.zh: 昔在漢世，諸呂自疑，內有硃虛、東牟之親，外有諸侯九國之強，故不敢動搖。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han age—various Lüs self doubted—inside had Zhuxu and Dongmou kin—outside had feudal lords nine states strong—therefore dared not shake move.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Lü clan hesitated because Liu kin and outer kings boxed them in.

sentences.zh: 於今之宜，諸侯強大，是為太山之固。

translations.literal: As for today's suitability—feudal lords strong large—this makes Mount Tai's solidity.
translations.idiomatic: Today strong princes are your Mount Tai bulwark.

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: Not our clan kind—their hearts surely different.
translations.idiomatic: "Alien hearts breed alien plots"—the Spring and Autumn saw it.

sentences.zh: 而魏法禁錮諸王，親戚隔絕，不祥莫大焉。

translations.literal: Yet Wei law imprisoned shackled various kings—kin relatives cut off separation—no ill greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei caged princes and severed kin—no worse omen.

sentences.zh: 間者無故又瓜分天下，立五等諸侯。

translations.literal: Recently without cause again carved divide All under Heaven—establish five ranks various feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Lately you carved the realm again into five noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 上不象賢，下不議功，而是非雜糅，例受茅土。

translations.literal: Above they did not emulate the worthy, below they did not deliberate on merit; yet right and wrong were mixed together, and [all], by rule, received fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Those at court did not look to exemplars for how to behave, nor did merit matter in discussion at lower levels—but right and wrong were jumbled anyway, while everyone routinely took their share of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 似權時之宜，非經久之制，將遂不改，此亦煩擾之人，漸亂之階也。

translations.literal: It resembles expediency for the moment and is no lasting system; should it thereafter go unchanged forever, such [a policy] belongs to those occasions of nuisance and clutter, too: it is likewise the doorstep to gradual chaos.
translations.idiomatic: It looks like stopgap pragmatism, not enduring institutions. If nothing is ever corrected, restless officials will seize on every inconsistency, and disorder will creep in by degrees.

sentences.zh: 夫國之興也，由於九族親睦，黎庶協和；

translations.literal: As for the rise of states, [it arose] because the Nine Clans dwelt together in intimacy and harmony, and common folk were harmonious and cooperative.
translations.idiomatic: States flourish when imperial kin knit close ties and ordinary people pull together.

sentences.zh: 其衰也，在於骨肉疏絕，百姓離心。

translations.literal: As for its decline: [the fault lay] when bone and flesh [kin] drifted estranged apart, and the hundred surnames [the people] harbored departed hearts.
translations.idiomatic: States rot when flesh-and-blood kin grow cold and estranged and the populace loses heart altogether.

sentences.zh: 故夏邦不安，伊尹歸殷；

translations.literal: Therefore Xia's domain was restless, and Yi Yin withdrew to Yin [Shang];
translations.idiomatic: So when Xia could not govern its own realm, Yi Yin withdrew to Shang territory.

sentences.zh: 殷邦不和，呂氏入周。

translations.literal: Yin's domain lacked harmony, and the Lüs entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang fractured, ministers of the Lü line crossed over into Zhou.

sentences.zh: 殷監在於夏後，去事之誡，誠來事之鑒也。

translations.literal: Shang looked to Xia's posteriors as mirror; departing matters' caution is truly the mirror of coming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shang drew its moral from Xia's aftermath: what has already ended is genuinely the precedent for what comes next.

sentences.zh: 又陳曰：

translations.literal: [He] moreover presented in petition, stating:
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized further, saying,

sentences.zh: 昔伐蜀，募取涼州兵馬、羌胡健兒，許以重報，五千餘人，隨艾討賊，功皆第一。

translations.literal: Formerly during the Shu campaign they levied troops and mounts from Liang province, strong Qiang and Hu boys, promising them lavish reward; upwards of five thousand men followed Deng Ai to strike rebels, yet their feats all ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was overrun, recruits from Liangzhou—Qiang horsemen, Hu recruits—were summoned with extravagant promises of pay. More than five thousand accompanied Deng Ai, and each company earned top marks.

sentences.zh: 而《乙亥詔書》，州郡將督，不與中外軍同，雖在上功，無應封者。

translations.literal: Yet the 'Yihai' imperial edict: commander-governors in commanderies and prefectures were treated differently from inner and outer [central] armies; though [some] attained highest merit ranks, none qualified for investment [as lord].
translations.idiomatic: But the decree of Yihai set provincial generals apart from armies under the metropolitan command—even first-class feats did not merit a feudal patent.

sentences.zh: 唯金城太守楊欣所領兵，以逼江由之勢，得封者三十人。

translations.literal: Only the Soldiery led by Governor of Jincheng Yang Xin, by reason of the pressure they applied at the Jiangyou approach, had thirty men who received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the detachment of Jincheng governor Yang Xin, which pressed the Jiangyou corridor, saw thirty men actually ennobled.

sentences.zh: 自金城以西，非在欣部，無一人封者。

translations.literal: West of Jincheng, those not in Xin's section: not a single man was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jincheng, outside Xin's command, nobody was given a title at all.

sentences.zh: 苟在中軍之例，雖下功必侯；

translations.literal: If [they] fell under central-army precedent, though [only] lower merit [rank], they would necessarily [be made] marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Had the same men been tallied as central-army troops, even middling performance would have won them a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 如在州郡，雖功高不封，非所謂近不重施，遠不遺恩之謂也。

translations.literal: if [instead they served] amid province and prefecture, though merit was lofty [they went] uninvest—this misses what they call 'those near withhold no double bounty' and 'those distant leave no grace unspent.'
translations.idiomatic: Caught in the provincial tally, lofty deeds went unrewarded—which contradicts the principle that insiders should not be spared honors twice while outsiders go empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞魚懸由於甘餌，勇夫死於重報。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard fish hang [on the line] owing to sweet bait, and reckless men die for rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet bait hangs the fish; big pay draws brave men willing to gamble their necks.

sentences.zh: 故荊軻慕燕丹之義，專諸感闔閭之愛，匕首振于秦庭，吳刀耀於魚腹，視死如歸，豈不有由也哉！

translations.literal: Hence Jing Ke admired Crown Prince Dan of Yan's sense of righteousness; Zhuan Zhu responded to King Helü of Wu's favor; dagger-hand brandished in Qin courtyard, Wu blade glinted in fish belly—they viewed death like returning homeward—is it not rooted in motive!
translations.idiomatic: So Jing Ke answered Prince Dan's call, Zhuan Zhu repaid King Helü's esteem—one waved a dagger in the Qin court, the other drew a blade from a salted fish—and both met death as calmly as going home. Such deeds always have their reasons.

sentences.zh: 夫功名重賞，士之所競，不平致怨，由來久矣。

translations.literal: As for meritorious name and hefty reward—is what shi [gentlemen-officials] race for—unfairness arousing resentment has had a long pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: Glory and gold are what officers chase; jealousy over uneven reward is as old as government itself.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「屍鳩在桑，其子七兮。

translations.literal: The 'Odes' declares: '[The cuckoo-dove] Shijiu is in the mulberry; its chicks are seven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs reads: 'The turtle-dove rests in the mulberry; it nurtures seven chicks beneath its wings.'

sentences.zh: 淑人君子，其儀一兮。

translations.literal: The good man—the noble man—his demeanor stands one [the same];
translations.idiomatic: The virtuous man's bearing is steadfast and even.

sentences.zh: 」臣以為此等宜蒙爵封。

translations.literal: ' Your subject holds that persons of such kind ought likewise to receive lordly rank patent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant submits that men of this stature deserve feudal patents as well.'

sentences.zh: 灼前後陳事，輒見省覽。

translations.literal: Zhuo's serial memorials beforehand and afterward invariably met imperial review.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Zhuo spoke up earlier or later at court, his words reached the emperor's desk.

sentences.zh: 然身微宦孤，不見進序，乃取長假還鄉里。

translations.literal: Yet his person petty, his offices lacking kin backup, advancement and seniority unseen, thereby he seized extended leave to return hometown.
translations.idiomatic: But he lacked rank, lacked a patronage circle, saw no promotions, so he took indefinite leave for his home district.

sentences.zh: 臨去，遣息上表曰：

translations.literal: On quitting, he dispatched his heir to ascend a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he sent his son up with another memorial that read,

sentences.zh: 臣受恩三世，剖符守境，試用無績，沈伏數年，犬馬之力，無所復堪。

translations.literal: Your servant has received favor three successive reigns, split tally guarding frontiers—trial-duty without achievement, submerged unadvancing several years—the strength of humble dog horses [this subject] has none left to devote.
translations.idiomatic: I have borne three sovereigns' favor, wielded tally on the marches yet produced no deeds, sunk in office for seasons without rise—whatever strength a petty retainer retains is spent.

sentences.zh: 陛下弘廣納之聽，采狂夫之言，原臣侵官之罪，不問幹忤之愆，天地恩厚，於臣足矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty magnifies broad-ranging hearing, adopts wild men's words—pardons [me] infringing office-boundaries' crime, asks not after defiant remonstrance's offence—Heaven-earth's bounty runs deep; toward your servant indeed it suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty listens widely and weighs even a crank's counsel—forgiving my overstep of jurisdiction and never punishing my blunt defiance. Heaven and earth could heap no greater kindness on me.

sentences.zh: 臣聞忠臣之于其君，猶孝子之於其親：進則有欣然之慶，非貪官也；

translations.literal: Your servant hears that one's loyal servant to his sovereign is akin to one's filial son to his parents—advancing yields glad joyous celebration—not coveting salary;
translations.idiomatic: A faithful minister resembles a dutiful child: advancing to office sparks honest joy—not greed for place.

sentences.zh: 退則有戚然之憂，非懷祿也。

translations.literal: retreating then bears melancholy grieving—not cherishing stipend;
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office brings mourning faces—not clinginess to paychecks.

sentences.zh: 其意在於不忘光君榮親，情所不能已已者也。

translations.literal: that intent settles in forgetting not illuminating sovereign-parent's glory—they are circumstances passion cannot constrain itself.
translations.idiomatic: The point is only to brighten ruler and forbears—to stop would betray every feeling altogether.

sentences.zh: 臣伏自悼，私懷至恨：生長荒裔，而久在外任，自還抱疾，未嘗覲見，陛下竟不知臣何人，此臣之恨一也。

translations.literal: Your servant prostrate meditates mourning, harboring inward utmost regret-grievances: bred in wild borderlands yet long stationed outer commands; since returning I hold illness, never attended audience—your Majesty still knows not who your servant is: this grievance-number-one of servant.
translations.idiomatic: I mourn inwardly: raised beyond the pale yet always sent to distant posts—recalled only to fall ill, never summoned to court—so Your Majesty still does not know who I am. That is my first regret.

sentences.zh: 遭運會之世，值有事之時，而不能垂功名於竹帛，此臣之恨二也。

translations.literal: [I] encountered an age of turning fortune, seized an era of crises, yet could not suspend fame-merit atop bamboo slips and silk—that regret-number-two.
translations.idiomatic: I lived stirring times yet never carved deeds into the historians' slips—that is sorrow two.

sentences.zh: 逮事聖明之君，而尪悴羸劣，陳力又不能，當歸死於地下，此臣之恨三也。

translations.literal: Attending unto sage-luminous ruler, yet haggard shrunken lame-wasted—uttering strength yet unable—ought return death beneath earth—that regret-three.
translations.idiomatic: I serve a luminous throne while my body wastes—wish to exert myself yet cannot—weighs as if buried already—that is sorrow three.

sentences.zh: 哀二親早亡隕，兄弟並凋喪，孝敬無復施於家門，此臣之恨四也。

translations.literal: Lamenting two parents decayed early vanished, brethren together withered off—Filial Reverence obtains no farther stage at household-portal—that regret-four.
translations.idiomatic: Father and mother left early and brothers vanished too—nowhere remains to practise filial devotion—that is sorrow four.

sentences.zh: 夏之日忽以過，冬之夜尋復來，人生百歲，尚以為不足，而臣中年嬰災，此臣之恨五也。

translations.literal: Summer daylight suddenly has passed—winter night's turn again arrives—man's life century length still esteemed insufficient—but your servant mid-years bound disaster—that regret-five.
translations.idiomatic: Summer afternoons vanish overnight; winters return swiftly; a century still feels brief—yet midway I am blasted by affliction—that is sorrow five.

sentences.zh: 慚日月之所養，愧昊蒼而無報，此臣之所以懷五恨而歎息，臨歸路而自悼者也。

translations.literal: Ashamed beneath sun-month's nourishment, shamed confronting vast azure without repaying—this servant's rationale holding five regrets sighing mournful, confronting homeward-road self-mournful.
translations.idiomatic: I blush under sun and moon, shame myself before Heaven with nothing to repay—five resentments haunt me sighing toward the journey home.

sentences.zh: 語有之曰：「華言虛也，至言實也，苦言藥也，甘言疾也。

translations.literal: Speech has proverb stating: '[Showy] embellished speech is empty; ultimate speech is solid; bitter speech is medicine; sweet speech is illness.'
translations.idiomatic: The old saw runs: 'Flattery is hollow, depth is real, bitter counsel is physic, honeyed words are poison.'

sentences.zh: 」臣欲言天下太平，而靈龜神狐未見，仙芝萐莆未生，麒麟未遊乎靈禽之囿，鳳皇未儀於太極之庭，此臣之所以不敢華言而為佞者也。

translations.literal: ' Your servant wishes speak All-under-Heaven Great Peace, yet spirit-tortoise divine fox not appeared, transcendence-mushroom magic-reed not born, qilin not roamed spirit-birds' park, phoenix not displayed form at Grand Ultimate courtyard—this servant's basis for not daring florid speech and becoming sycophant.
translations.idiomatic: I would love to announce universal peace, but no tortoise omens, no lucky fungi, no qilin stalking the royal menagerie, no phoenix wheeling the inner court—so I cannot mouth pretty lies and play the flatterer.'

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖初定天下，于時戍卒婁敬上書諫曰：「陛下取天下不與成周同，而欲比靈斯成周，臣竊以為不侔。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gaozu first settled All-under-Heaven; at that time garrison-soldier Lou Jing ascended memorial remonstrating: 'Your Majesty taking the empire does not match Cheng-Zhou's way, yet wishes compare numinous-sublimity with Cheng-Zhou's completion—your servant privately holds [the two] unequal.'
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu had just pacified the realm, the conscript Lou Jing warned: 'You seized the realm differently from the Zhou founders, yet you want to match their spiritual perfection—I see no parity.'

sentences.zh: 」於是漢祖感悟，深納其言，賜姓為劉氏。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon Han's Ancestor sensed insight, deeply ingested his words, bestowed him surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took the lesson, swallowed the advice whole, and ennobled Lou Jing as a Liu.

sentences.zh: 又顧謂陸賈曰：「為我著秦所以亡，而吾所以得之者。

translations.literal: Further he turned declaring to Lu Jia: 'For me compose how Qin perished—and how myself obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: He likewise told Lu Jia: 'Draft for me why Qin fell and why I survived.'

sentences.zh: 」賈乃作《新語》之書，述敘前世成敗，以為勸戒。

translations.literal: ' Jia thereupon authored 'New Discourses'-book—narrating former generations success-failure to serve advising caution.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia then wrote New Discourses, laying out successive dynasties' rises and crashes as cautionary mirror.'

sentences.zh: 又田肯建一言之計，非親子弟莫可使王齊者，而受千金之賜。

translations.literal: Further Tian Ken proposed one-utterance stratagem—not blood kin offspring none may be sent prince-over Qi—and received thousand-catty gold reward-grant.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ken's single blunt warning—that only imperial sons should rule Qi—won him gold measured by the thousand-piece.

sentences.zh: 故世稱漢祖之寬明博納，所以能成帝業也。

translations.literal: Thus the age lauded Han Ancestor's broad enlightened vast acceptance—whereby succeeded completing imperial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Hence posterity praises Gaozu's spacious mind—how else could the Han dynasty have cohered?

sentences.zh: 今之言世者，皆曰堯舜復興，天下已太平矣。

translations.literal: Those who speak nowadays of generations all pronounce Yao-Shun anew reborn—all-under-heaven already Great Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Modern chatter insists Yao and Shun have returned and peace reigns outright.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為未，亦竊有所勸焉。

translations.literal: Your servant alone holds not-thus—also covertly lodges counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I alone dissent—and still venture counsel.

sentences.zh: 且百王垂制，聖賢吐言，來事之明鑒也。

translations.literal: Moreover hundred monarchs dangling institutions, saints worthies spit-forth doctrines—forthcoming affair's luminous mirror lies therein.
translations.idiomatic: Countless rulers left institutions; sages left maxims—all are mirrors for posterity.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「堯不能以天下與舜，則舜之有天下也，天與之也。

translations.literal: Mencius states: '[Even] Yao cannot bestow empire on Shun—so Shun possessing empire arose from Heaven gifting.'
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: Not even Yao could hand empire to Shun outright—his throne was Heaven's gift.'

sentences.zh: 昔舜為相，堯崩，三年之喪畢，舜避堯之子于南河，天下諸侯朝覲者、獄訟者，不之堯之子而之舜。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun acted minister—Yao perished—the three-years mourning finished—Shun avoided Yao's son south of southern River—realm's nobles dukes who court-paid, who plead lawsuits, proceeded not unto Yao's son but proceeded unto Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun was minister and Yao died, after mourning Shun withdrew south of the river; lords bearing tribute and plaintiffs seeking judgments sought Shun rather than Yao's heir.'

sentences.zh: 舜曰天也，乃之中國，踐天子位焉。

translations.literal: Shun proclaimed 'Heaven;' then he entered Middle Region, trod heavenly-son throne.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing Heaven's mandate, Shun returned to the heartland and mounted the throne.'

sentences.zh: 若居堯之宮，逼堯之子，非天所與者也。

translations.literal: If [he] dwelt Yao's palace, pressed Yao's son—[that] is not Heaven's conferral.
translations.idiomatic: Had he squatted in Yao's halls and bullied Yao's son, that would not be Heaven's gift.'

sentences.zh: 」曩昔西有不臣之蜀，東有僭號之吳，三主鼎足，並稱天子。

translations.literal: ' Long-ago west held non-subject Shu—east held usurping-title Wu—three lords tripod-footed—together styled Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Shu in the west withheld allegiance, Wu in the east proclaimed its own reign, and three thrones stood tripod-wise, each daring the title Son of Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 魏文帝率萬乘之眾，受禪於靡陂，而自以德同唐、虞，以為漢獻即是古之堯，自謂即是今之舜，乃謂孟柯、孫卿不通禪代之變，遂作禪代之文，刻石垂戒，班示天下，傳之後世，亦安能使將來君子皆曉然心服其義乎！

translations.literal: Wei Wendi led myriad-chariots' host, received abdication at Mipi-bank—yet himself thought virtue matched Tang-Yu—deemed Han Xiandi equaled archaic Yao—self-deemed equaled present Shun—then pronounced Meng Ke, Sun Qing unversed shan-dai's vicissitudes—thereupon authored shan-dai's text, carved stone hanging caution, promulgated displayed all-under-heaven, transmitted posterity generations—how could it make yet-to-come noble men all clearly grasp heart-convinced its righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao Pi brought an army of ten thousand chariots to Mipi to take the abdication—then styled himself Yao and Shun reborn, cast Emperor Xian as ancient Yao, himself as modern Shun, dismissed Mencius and Xunzi for missing the point of abdication, carved his own charter in stone, and broadcast it as eternal law—how could that ever persuade future gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 然魏文徒希慕堯、舜之名，推新集之魏，欲以同于唐、虞之盛，忽骨肉之恩，忘籓屏之固，竟不能使四海賓服，混一皇化，而于時群臣莫有諫者，不其過矣哉！

translations.literal: Yet Wei Wendi vainly yearned Yao-Shun's names, pushed fresh-convened Wei, wished match Tang-Yu's splendor—overlooked bone-flesh favor-forgot barricade-screen's solidity—ultimately could not make four seas guest-submit, merge-unify imperial transformation—while at that time assembled ministers none remonstrated—was that not excess-fault!
translations.idiomatic: He only aped the labels of Yao and Shun, forced a brand-new Wei, and imagined rivaling the golden age—while casting aside kinship and crumbling the walls of princely support. The realm never truly bowed, unification never arrived, and not one minister dared object—what a failure!

sentences.zh: 孫卿曰：「堯、舜禪讓，是不然矣。

translations.literal: Sun Qing states: 'Yao-Shun abdication-shan-rang—this is not so.'
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi declared: 'The tale of Yao and Shun peacefully yielding the throne is simply wrong.'

sentences.zh: 天下者，至重也，非至強莫之能任；

translations.literal: As for all-under-heaven—it is utmost weight—without utmost strength none can bear it;
translations.idiomatic: The realm is the heaviest burden—only the mightiest can shoulder it.

sentences.zh: 至大也，非至辯莫之能分；

translations.literal: utmost vastness—without utmost eloquence none can divide it;
translations.idiomatic: It is the broadest domain—only the clearest debater can parse it.

sentences.zh: 至眾也，非至明莫之能見。

translations.literal: utmost multitude—without utmost luminosity none can survey it.
translations.idiomatic: It is the teeming mass—only the sharpest eye can oversee it.

sentences.zh: 此三至者，非聖人莫之能盡。

translations.literal: These three utmosts—without sage none can exhaust them.'
translations.idiomatic: None but a sage can master all three.'

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，孫卿、孟軻亦各有所不取焉。

translations.literal: From this speaking, Sun Qing, Meng Ke each also possessed what they did not adopt.
translations.idiomatic: So Xunzi and Mencius each declined part of the other's lesson.

sentences.zh: 陛下受禪，從東府入西宮，兵刃耀天，旌旗翳日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received abdication—east quarter entered west palace—arms' blades gleamed heaven—banners' flags eclipsed sun.
translations.idiomatic: When you took the throne you marched from the eastern offices into the western palace—blades flashed sky-high, standards blotted out the sun.

sentences.zh: 雖應天順人，同符唐、虞，然法度損益，則亦不異于昔魏文矣，故宜資三至以強制之。

translations.literal: Though responding Heaven obeying men, tokens matching Tang-Yu—yet laws' measures' cuts-additions then also differed not from former Wei Wendi—therefore ought draw on three-utmosts to strengthen coercing it.
translations.idiomatic: Though you answered Heaven and the people like the ancient model, the legal adjustments differed little from Cao Pi's coup—so you must lean on Xunzi's three 'utmosts' to brace the state.

sentences.zh: 而今諸王有立國之名，而無襟帶之實。

translations.literal: Yet now the host of royals possess founding-state's name—yet lack breast-sash girdle-belt's substance.
translations.idiomatic: Today the kings bear state titles but none hold real border command like a true girdle around the capital.

sentences.zh: 又蜀地有自然之險，是曆世奸雄之所窺覦，逋逃之所聚也，而無親戚子弟之守，此豈深思遠慮，杜漸防萌者乎！

translations.literal: Further Shu territory possesses nature's dangerous defiles—this is successive generations' treacherous heroes' object of covetous gaze, fugitives' place of gathering—yet lacks kinsmen posterity son-nephews' guard—how can this be deep pondering far planning, damming seepage preventing buds!
translations.idiomatic: Shu is a natural fortress every warlord envies and every rebel flees toward—yet no imperial kinsman holds it. Is that prudent foresight or choke-point policy?

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝據已成之業，六合同風，天下一家。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wendi leaned on already-complete enterprise—six directions shared one wind—all-under-heaven single household.
translations.idiomatic: Even Han Wendi ruled an empire already knitted into one breeze, one hearth.

sentences.zh: 而賈誼上疏陳當時之勢，猶以為譬如抱火厝於積薪之下，而寢其上，火未及然，因謂之安。

translations.literal: Yet Jia Yi ascended memorial outlining that hour's tendencies—still likened circumstance to clasping flame placing pile-on kindling below—upon it sleeping fire not yet flaming—accordingly deeming-it secure.
translations.idiomatic: Still Jia Yi warned Wen was cuddling glowing coals piled on firewood while declaring himself safe.

sentences.zh: 此言誠存不忘亡，安不忘亂者也。

translations.literal: This speech truly preserved not-forgetting perdition amid peace, tranquility not-forgetting tumult.
translations.idiomatic: That is candor remembering ruin in security and unrest in calm.

sentences.zh: 然臣之慺慺，亦竊願陛下居安思危，無曰高高在上，常念臨深之義，不忘履冰之戒。

translations.literal: Yet servant's sincerity-sincere also secretly desires Your Majesty dwell peace ponder peril—speak-not 'loftily lofty above' forever—often reflect facing-deep's duty-not-forget treading ice's injunction.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to presume you sit too high forever—dwell on vertigo beside a cliff and ice underfoot.

sentences.zh: 盡除魏世之弊法，綏以新政之大化，使萬邦欣欣，喜戴洪惠，昆蟲草木，咸蒙恩澤。

translations.literal: Exhaust-removing Wei-era's harm-laws—pacify-using new governance's great transformation—make myriad regions bliss-bliss joyous—joyfully carry Great Bounty—even insects grasses trees all soak grace-moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Scrub Wei malpractice, widen your new statutes until every kingdom sings and even bugs and grasses drink your bounty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷詠康哉之歌，山藪無伐檀之人，此固天下所視望者也。

translations.literal: Court recites Tranquility-song's hymns—hill-grove possesses none felling '[Zhan]Tan' fellows—this solidly constitutes all-under-heaven's object of expectancy-gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Let the halls echo the hymn of orderly rule and the hills harbour no starving woodcutter—that is what the empire watches for.

sentences.zh: 陛下自初踐阼，發無諱之詔，置箴諫之官，赫然寵異諤諤之臣，以明好直言之信，恐陳事者知直言之不用，皆杜口結舌，祥瑞亦曷由來哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty from first treading throne platform issued no-taboo edict—installed admonition-remonstrance officials—brilliantly favored distinct outspoken ministers—to clarify loving straight-speech's trust—lest memorializers know straight-speech unemployed—all seal-mouth knot-tongue—auspicious portents moreover how whereby arrive!
translations.idiomatic: From your very accession you invited blunt counsel and prized outspoken aides—yet if plain advice is quietly shelved tongues knot shut and auspicious omens never arrive anyway!

sentences.zh: 臣無陸生之才，不在顧問之地，蓋聞主聖臣直，義在於有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Your servant lacks Lu-born's talents—not located counsel-inquiry precinct—generally hear lord sage minister straight—duty resides having offence lacking concealment.
translations.idiomatic: I am no Lu Jia—you did not summon me—but the maxim holds: under a sage king ministers must speak straight even when it hurts.

sentences.zh: 臣不惟疏遠，未信而言，敢曆論前代隆名之君及亡敗之主廢興所由，又博陳舉賢之路，廣開養老之制，崇必信之道，又張設議者之難，凡五事以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant not-only remote-estranged, un-trusted yet speaking—dares traverse-discuss anterior generations lofty-name rulers and perdition-collapsed rulers' rise-fall causal-chains—further broadly presents raising-worthies's roadways—broad-opening nursing-elderlies' systems—elevate surely-trusted way—again arrays debaters's difficulties—all five affairs to memorialize-report.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am insignificant and unheard, I will survey famous rises and rotten falls, map paths for talent, widen care for elders, reaffirm sincerity, rehearse objections—five headings in all.

sentences.zh: 臣之所言，皆直陳古今已行故事，非新聲異端也。

translations.literal: That which your servant utters—all straight-announce ancient-present already-practiced precedents—not new-tone heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing here is novelty—only what history already tried.

sentences.zh: 辭義實淺，不足採納。

translations.literal: Diction righteousness truly shallow—not worth picking accepting.
translations.idiomatic: My phrasing stays thin—barely worthy of inclusion.

sentences.zh: 然臣私心，誠謂有可發起覺悟遺忘。

translations.literal: Yet servant's private heart sincerely holds feasible rousing awaken forgotten-lapses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hope scraps of it jog what memory forgets.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣愚忠，湣臣狂直，無使天下以言者為戒。

translations.literal: Willing Your Majesty inspect servant ignorant loyalty—pity servant mad straight—cause-not all-under-heaven deem speech-makers-warning.
translations.idiomatic: Please read this dull loyalty kindly so the world learns blunt words are safe.

sentences.zh: 疾痛增篤，退念桑梓之詩，惟狐死之義，輒取長休，歸近墳墓。

translations.literal: Ill-pain aggravated severe—draw back pondering mulberry-fields' ode—ponder fox-death righteousness—accordingly seize extended resting—return approaching grave-mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Pain worsened; I heed the hymn of homecomings and the maxim that foxes prefer their birthplace—long leave it is so I might die near ancestral tombs.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宮闕，系情皇極，不勝丹款，遣息穎表言。

translations.literal: Glancing imperial-palaces—heart bound sagely-pole—not overcome cinnabar candidness—dispatch heir Ying ascend memorial speech.
translations.idiomatic: My eyes cling to palace gates though my spine fails—so I risk honesty through my son Ying's pen.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：臣聞善有章也，著在經典；

translations.literal: First item declares: Your servant hears good possessing manifest rules—indelibly fixed in scriptures-classics;
translations.idiomatic: First: deeds of good lie spelled out in the canon.

sentences.zh: 惡有罰也，戒在刑書。

translations.literal: evil possessing penalties—warnings reside criminal codices.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongs live under the lash of written law.

sentences.zh: 上自遠古，下洎秦、漢，其明王霸主及亡國暗君，故可得而稱；

translations.literal: Above from remote antiquity, below descending to Qin Han—those luminous kings hegemons and extinguished-country dim rulers—for these one can obtain appellations;
translations.idiomatic: From farthest antiquity through Qin and Han you can tally bright rulers, dark losers, conquerors gone under.

sentences.zh: 至於忠蹇賢相及佞諂奸臣，亦可得而言。

translations.literal: stretching unto loyal arduous worthy chancellors and fawning crafty evil ministers—for these likewise one can articulate.
translations.idiomatic: You can also name steadfast ministers beside conniving villains.

sentences.zh: 故朝有諤諤盡規之臣，無不昌也；

translations.literal: Therefore court possessing outspoken blunt exhaust-regulation ministers—never not flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Courts stocked with quarrelsome straight men always flourished.

sentences.zh: 任用阿諛唯唯之士，無不亡也。

translations.literal: employing yielding flattery yes-yes gents—never not perished.
translations.idiomatic: Courts manned by yes-men vanished without exception.

sentences.zh: 是有國者皆欲求忠以自輔，舉賢以自佐；

translations.literal: Those possessing states altogether wish seek loyalty to assist self—elevate worthy to aid self;
translations.idiomatic: Every sovereign wants loyalty to prop him up and genius to sharpen him.

sentences.zh: 而亡國破家者相繼，皆由任失其人。

translations.literal: yet perdition-collapsed ruined-house ones succeed one-after-another—altogether stemming from employing losing its proper men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruin follows ruin because the wrong faces fill the mats.

sentences.zh: 所謂賢者不賢，忠者不忠也。

translations.literal: What is termed worthy—is not worthy; termed loyal—not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: They call allies worthy who are worthless, loyal who are thieves.

sentences.zh: 臣謹言前任賢所由興，任不肖所以亡者。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully recounts predecessors' employing worthies causal rise, employing unworthies causal fall.
translations.idiomatic: I recount how predecessors rose on talent and sank on villains.

sentences.zh: 堯之末年，四凶在朝而不去，八元在家而不舉，然致天平地寧，四門穆穆，其功固在重華之為相。

translations.literal: Yao's late years—the four fierce ones stationed court yet departed not—the eight perfected ones lodged home yet summoned not—nevertheless effected heaven-flat earth tranquillity—four Gates augustly majestic—whose achievement solidly lodged in Chonghua's functioning minister.
translations.idiomatic: Late Yao let four beasts squat in council while ignoring the Eight Paragons, yet harmony held—credit belongs to Shun as minister.

sentences.zh: 夏癸放於鳴條，商辛梟於牧野，此俱萬乘之主，而國滅身擒，由不能屬任賢相，用婦人之言，荒淫無道，肆志沈宴，作靡靡之樂，長夜之飲，於是登糟丘，臨酒池，觀牛飲，望肉林，龍逢忠而被害，比干諫而剖心，天下之所以歸惡者也。

translations.literal: Jie of Xia was driven out at Mingtiao—Xin of Shang had his severed head displayed at Muye—these jointly myriad-chariot's lords—yet state extinguished body seized—stemming from inability consecrate-assign worthy minister—employing woman's speech—dissolute riot lacking way license-will drowned feast—composed wan-wan melodies—drawn-out night's drinking—thereupon ascending lees mound—overlooking wine pool—surveying cattle guzzling—gazing carnal forest—Guan Longpang loyal yet suffered harm—Bi Gan remonstrating yet torso cleaved—all-under-heaven's cause for returning malignance.
translations.idiomatic: Jie of Xia ended in defeat at Mingtiao; Zhou of Shang hung as a trophy at Muye—each commanded ten thousand chariots yet lost throne and life for heeding women rather than ministers, wallowing in debauch: mounds of mash, pools of wine, oxen drinking like men, groves of roasting meat—until loyal Guan Longpang died for speaking truth and blunt Bi Gan lost his heart—all under Heaven turned their hatred toward them.

sentences.zh: 太甲暴虐，顛覆湯之典制，於是伊尹放之桐宮，而能改悔反善，三年而後歸於亳。

translations.literal: Tai Jia riot-cruel—overturned Tang's statutes—thereupon Yi Yin expelled him to the Tong Palace—and could reform regret turn good—three years afterward returned toward Bo-capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia trampled Tang's ordinances, so Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace until he repented; three years later he restored him to Bo, the royal seat.

sentences.zh: 既已放而復還，殷道微而復興，諸侯咸服，號稱太宗，實賴阿衡之盡忠也。

translations.literal: Already once expelled afterward again returned—Yin-way declined-yet anew prospered—all nobles together submitted—designation styled Grand Ancestor—solidly leaned on A-heng Yi Yin's exhaust-loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Once restored, the Shang line rallied from decline and every lord submitted; he earned the temple epithet Taizong—thanks wholly to Yi Yin's single-minded devotion.

sentences.zh: 周室既衰，諸侯並爭，天王微弱，政遂陵遲。

translations.literal: Zhou house already declined—nobles feudatories together quarreled—heaven king frail weakened—government thereupon hillside-slipped tardy-decayed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou sank, feudatories warred together, kings grew feeble and policy slid downhill.

sentences.zh: 齊桓公，淫亂之主耳；

translations.literal: Qi Huan Gong—dissolute turbulent ruler ear;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi lived as a voluptuary.

sentences.zh: 然所以能九合一匡之功，有尊周之名，誠管夷吾之力。

translations.literal: yet whereby could nine alliances one rectification merits—hold honouring Zhou's fame—truthfully steward-yi Zhong's power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he knit nine alliances and forced order on the empire—chiefly because of Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，蟲流出門，豈非任豎貂之過乎！

translations.literal: Reaching unto his demise—worm-maggots oozed out gate—could it lack appointing Shu Diao fault!
translations.idiomatic: Dead, his corpse maggotted into the hallway—surely Shu Diao's fault.

sentences.zh: 且一桓公之身，得管仲，其功如彼；

translations.literal: Moreover one Huan Gong torso—obtained Guan Zhong—his feats like-so;
translations.idiomatic: The same man's body—with Guan Zhong he soared.

sentences.zh: 用豎貂，其亂如此。

translations.literal: employing Shu Diao—his turbulence like-this.
translations.idiomatic: With Shu Diao he crashed.

sentences.zh: 夫榮辱存亡，實在所任，可不審哉！

translations.literal: As for glory-shame perdurance-extinction—in truth settles on whom entrusted—might one not scrutinize attentively!
translations.idiomatic: Glory or ruin hinges on ministers chosen—inspect that choice fiercely.

sentences.zh: 秦本伯翳之後，微微小邑，至秦仲始大，有車馬禮樂侍御之好焉。

translations.literal: Qin's root descended Boyi's posteriors—minute minute tiny walled-place—until Qin Zhong first enlarged—having chariot-horse ritual-music attendant-guards' beauties therein.
translations.idiomatic: Qin traced back to Boyi—once a petty stockade—until Zhong enlarged it toward chariotry and court music.

sentences.zh: 自穆公至於始皇，皆能留心待賢，遠求異士，招由余於西戎，致五羖于宛市，取丕豹于晉鄉，迎蹇叔于宗裏。

translations.literal: From Duke Mu stretching unto First Emperor—all could devote heart awaiting worthies—far seek uncommon gentlemen—summon You Yu amidst western Rong—deliver Five Black Rams unto Wan market—capture Pi Leopard within Jin outskirts—welcome Jian Shu at Zong village.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Mu onward every ruler hunted talent—You Yu from the west, five rams swapped in Nanyang, Pi Leopard torn from Jin, Jian Shu coaxed down from Zong village.

sentences.zh: 由是四方雄俊繼踵而至，故能世為強國，吞滅諸侯，奄有天下，兼稱皇帝，由謀臣之助也。

translations.literal: From this, heroes and outstanding men from the four directions came following heel upon heel; therefore [Qin] could generation after generation be a mighty state, swallow and annihilate the feudal lords, embrace possession of All Under Heaven, and concurrently style itself Emperor—this was because of the assistance of its counsellors.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, brave and capable men flocked in from every quarter, so that Qin could remain a great power for generations: it devoured the regional states, held the whole realm, and took the imperial title as well—and all of that rested on the strength of its strategists.

sentences.zh: 道化未淳，崩於沙丘。

translations.literal: The transforming influence of the Way was not yet pure; [he] collapsed at Sandy Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Moral transformation had not yet settled when the First Emperor died at Shaqiu.

sentences.zh: 胡亥乘虐，用詐自悮，不能弘濟統緒，克成堂構，而乃殘賊仁義，毒流黔首。

translations.literal: Hu Hai rode upon cruelty, employed deceit and misled himself, was unable broadly to sustain the main line of succession and successfully complete the hall-and-rafters legacy, and instead cruelly injured benevolence and righteousness, so poison spread to the black-haired commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Ershi rode his father's violence, schemed his way to the throne and trapped himself, failed to shore up the legitimate line of rule or finish the edifice his father had raised, and instead trampled human decency until its venom seeped through the common people.

sentences.zh: 故陳勝、吳廣，奮臂大呼，而天下回應。

translations.literal: Therefore Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised their arms and cried aloud, and All Under Heaven answered in response.
translations.idiomatic: So Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised their fists and shouted to the world, and the empire answered from every side.

sentences.zh: 於是趙高逆亂，閻樂承指，二世窮迫，自戮望夷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Gao rebelled in disorder, Yan Le received his finger[-pointed command], the Second Generation was driven to extremity, and at Wangyi [palace] killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao Gao turned traitor, Yan Le did his bidding, the Second Emperor was cornered, and cut his own throat at Wangyi.

sentences.zh: 子嬰雖立，去帝為王，孤危無輔，四旬而亡。

translations.literal: Although Ziying was installed, [he] removed the title of emperor and styled himself king; orphaned and imperilled with none to aid [him]; in forty days [he] perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziying finally took charge he demoted himself from emperor to mere king—too isolated and too late—and within forty days the house was gone.

sentences.zh: 此由邪臣擅命，指鹿為馬，所以速秦之禍也。

translations.literal: This was because wicked ministers monopolised commands, pointed at a deer and called it a horse—therefore they hastened Qin's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Vicious favourites seized the government, called a deer a horse, and in doing so they hurried Qin to its ruin.

sentences.zh: 秦失其鹿，豪傑競逐，項羽既得而失之，其咎在烹韓生，而范增之謀不用。

translations.literal: Qin lost its deer; heroes strove in competition. Xiang Yu grasped it yet lost it; his fault lay in boiling Han Sheng alive, and in Fan Zeng's stratagems going unused.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin dropped the prize, every warlord lunged for it. Xiang Yu seized the advantage and threw it away—blame the execution of his honest adviser Han Sheng and his refusal to heed Fan Zeng.

sentences.zh: 假令羽既距項伯之邪說，斬沛公於鴻門，都咸陽以號令諸侯，則天下無敵矣。

translations.literal: Supposing Yu had already rejected Xiang Bo's perverse counsel, beheaded the Duke of Pei at Hongmen, and established his capital at Xianyang to command the feudal lords—then All Under Heaven would have had no match.
translations.idiomatic: Had he brushed aside Xiang Bo's bad advice, killed Liu Bang at the Hongmen banquet, and ruled from Xianyang with a finger on every rival, no one in the realm could have stood against him.

sentences.zh: 而羽距韓生之忠諫，背范增之深計，自謂霸王之業已定，都彭城，還故鄉，為晝被文繡，此蓋世俗兒女之情耳，而羽榮之。

translations.literal: Yet Yu refused Han Sheng's loyal remonstrance, turned his back on Fan Zeng's deep plans, fancied himself already settled in his hegemon-king enterprise, chose Pengcheng as his capital, returned to his home region, and by day draped himself in patterned embroidery—this is merely the sentiment of vulgar sons and daughters, yet Yu gloried in it.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he spurned Han Sheng's blunt counsel, ignored Fan Zeng's designs, decided the hegemony was already his, lounged back in Pengcheng and his native haunt, flaunting brocaded silks like a suburban parvenu—and he preened over it.

sentences.zh: 是故五載為漢所擒，至此尚不知覺悟，乃曰「天亡我，非戰之罪」，甚痛矣哉！

translations.literal: Therefore within five years he was captured by Han; arriving at this point he still knew no awakening, and proclaimed, 'Heaven destroys me—it is no fault of war'—how very painful!
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Han had him bound, and even then his only excuse was ‘Heaven has doomed me—not my generalship!’—there is bitterness in hearing it.

sentences.zh: 且夫士之歸仁，猶水之歸下，禽之走曠野，故曰「為川驅魚者獺也，為藪驅雀者鸇也，為湯、武驅人者桀、紂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, shi who turn toward benevolence are like water tending downward or birds fleeing to the wilds; hence it is said, 'Those who for the rivers drive the fish are the otters; those who for the marsh drive the finches are the sparrowhawks; those who for Tang and Wu herd the people are Jie and Zhou.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, gentlemen flock to humane rule as water runs downhill or game seeks open ground. The classic line runs: ‘Otters harry fish into the deep pools; goshawks harry sparrows into the brush; tyrants like Jie and Zhou chase the people straight into the arms of founders like Tang and Wu.’

sentences.zh: 」漢高祖起于布衣，提三尺之刃而取天下，用六國之資，無唐、虞之禪，豈徒賴良、平之奇謀，盡英雄之智力而已乎，亦由項 氏為驅人也。

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. Han Gaozu arose from coarse cloth, grasped a three-foot blade and took All Under Heaven, employed the resources of the six states, had no abdications like those of Tang or Yu—how could it be merely that he relied on the singular schemes of [Zhang] Liang and [Chen] Ping and exhausted the wits of every hero? It was likewise because the Xiang clan drove the people [to him].
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han began as a commoner, took up a short sword, and won the realm with the wealth of the six former kingdoms—there was no gracious handover like the legends of Yao and Shun. His victory was not only Zhang Liang's and Chen Ping's cunning or the muscle of every adventurer; the Xiang clan itself herded the population into Liu Bang's camp.

sentences.zh: 子孫承基二百餘年，逮成帝委政舅家，使權勢外移。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons inherited the foundation for more than two hundred years, until it reached Emperor Cheng, who delegated government to his maternal uncles' house and caused power and influence to shift outward.
translations.idiomatic: His line held the mandate for over two centuries until Emperor Cheng handed the real work to his mother's kin and watched real authority drift beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 安昌侯張禹者，漢之三公，成帝保傅也，帝親幸其家，拜禹床下，深問天災人事。

translations.literal: Marquis Anchang Zhang Yu was one of Han's Three Dukes and Emperor Cheng's guardian-tutor; the Emperor personally favoured his house, bowed below Zhang Yu's couch, and deeply inquired about Heaven's calamities and human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu of Anchang sat among the three highest ministers and had nursed Emperor Cheng as tutor; the sovereign made personal calls on his estate, kowtowed beneath the old man's daybed, and pressed him for guidance on portents and policy.

sentences.zh: 禹當惟大臣之節，為社稷深慮，忠言嘉謀，陳其災患，則王氏不得專權寵，王莽無緣乘勢位，遂托雲龍而登天衢，令漢祚中絕也。

translations.literal: Yu ought to have upheld a great minister's integrity, deeply pondered for the altars of soil and grain, offered loyal words and excellent plans, set forth its disasters and worries—then the Wang clan could not have monopolised favour and power, Wang Mang would have lacked a chance to ride momentum and rank, ascend by the cloud-dragon metaphor to the celestial thoroughfares, and cause Han's imperial fortune to snap mid-course.
translations.idiomatic: A man in his station should have spoken for the dynasty, weighed the fate of the altars in good faith, and laid the dangers plain; if he had, the Wangs could never have hoarded every lever, Wang Mang would never have climbed the dragon's mist into power, and the Han mandate might not have broken halfway.

sentences.zh: 禹佞諂不忠，挾懷私計，徒低仰于五侯之間，苟取容媚而已。

translations.literal: Yu was sycophantic and unfaithful, harboured private calculations, merely lowered and raised his head among the Five Marquises, and crudely sought favour and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Zhang Yu flattered his way through the Wang circle, trimming his sails between the Five Marquises and angling only for smiles from the throne.

sentences.zh: 是以硃雲抗節求尚方斬馬劍，欲以斬禹，以戒其餘，可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhu Yun, upholding integrity, demanded the Shangfang [imperial armory] sword for beheading horses, intending to behead Yu, to warn the rest—this can be called loyal.
translations.idiomatic: So Zhu Yun defied protocol to demand the palace armory's horse-beheading blade, ready to strike Zhang Yu's head off as an example—it was fidelity of the courageous sort.

sentences.zh: 而成帝尚復不寤，乃以為居下訕上，廷辱保傅，罪死無赦，詔御史將雲下，欲急烹之。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Cheng still did not awake; indeed he judged it railing from below upon those above and court insult to guardian-tutors—as a crime deserving death without pardon—and ordered the censor escort Yun down [to judgement], intending to boil him hurriedly.
translations.idiomatic: Even then Emperor Cheng would not wake up: Zhu Yun was somehow a criminal for shaming tutor and emperor alike, deserved execution without appeal, so the clerks hurried him toward the boiling cauldron.

sentences.zh: 雲攀殿折檻，幸賴左將軍辛慶忌叩頭流血，以死爭之。

translations.literal: Yun clung to the palace hall and broke the threshold; fortunately he relied on General of the Left Xin Qingji knocking his head until it bled, contending for him with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun had to clutch the hall balustrade and snap the marble rail before General of the Left Xin Qingji could batter his brow bloody and buy his life with his own safety.

sentences.zh: 若不然，則雲已摧碎矣。

translations.literal: Had it not been so, then Yun would already have been shattered to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Without that intervention he would have been torn apart on the spot.

sentences.zh: 後雖釋檻不修，欲以彰明直臣，誠足以為後世之戒，何益於漢室所由亡也哉！

translations.literal: Although afterwards [the court] released [him from] the stock and did not repair [the threshold], intending thereby to display the upright minister, truly it may suffice as a warning for later ages—what benefit had it for the reason Han house thereby perished!
translations.idiomatic: Later they left the broken rail unrepaired to advertise a straight speaker—fine theatre for the chronicles, but it did nothing to cure the illness that would kill Han.

sentences.zh: 然世之論者以為亂臣賊子無道之甚者莫過於莽，此亦猶紂之不善不如是之甚也。

translations.literal: Yet debaters of the age judge that among disorderly ministers and unfilial sons none without the Way exceeded Mang to such a degree—this too is like saying Zhou [Xin]'s wickedness did not reach such an extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Later writers treat Wang Mang as the worst traitor imaginable, much as moralists pretend King Zhou's evil was unmatched—both judgments overstate the case.

sentences.zh: 傳稱莽始起外戚，折節力行，以要名譽，宗族稱孝，朋友歸仁。

translations.literal: The tradition states that Mang at first arose from maternal relatives, bent his demeanour and exerted conduct, thereby to seek reputation; his lineage kin called him filial, friends returned to his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Records say Wang Mang began as an in-law who cosplayed austerity, curried a spotless name until kinsmen praised his filial piety and friends swore to his kindness.

sentences.zh: 及其輔政成、哀之際，勤勞國家，動見稱述。

translations.literal: When it reached his assisting government at the juncture of Emperors Cheng and Ai, he toiled for the state, and in action he was praised and recounted.
translations.idiomatic: By the Cheng and Ai reigns he looked busy on the state's behalf, and every gesture drew applause from the chroniclers.

sentences.zh: 然于時人士詣闕上書薦莽者不可稱紀，內外群臣莫不歸莽功德。

translations.literal: Yet at that time gentlemen who went to the palace gate to submit memorials recommending Mang could not be fully recorded, and among inner and outer ministers none failed to attribute merit and virtue to Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials praising him stacked up at the palace gate faster than anyone could count, and every courtier, inside or out, sang of his genius and virtue.

sentences.zh: 遭遇漢室中微，國嗣三絕，而太后壽考，為之宗主，故莽得遂策命孺子而奪其位也。

translations.literal: Meeting Han house in mid-decline, the imperial heir three times cut off, while the Grand Empress Dowager enjoyed long years and served as its ritual head—therefore Mang could carry out the abdication edict for the child emperor and wrest his throne.
translations.idiomatic: Han was already hollow, the succession had failed three times over, and the aged Grand Empress Dowager remained the ritual figurehead—so Mang could stage the script for the boy ruler and walk off with the talisman.

sentences.zh: 昔湯、武之興，亦逆取而順守之耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang's and Wu's rise likewise took by revolt yet preserved by compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Even Tang and Wu had seized power by force before they secured it through just rule.

sentences.zh: 向莽深惟殷、周取守之術，崇道德，務仁義，履信實，去華偽，施惠天下，十有八年，恩足以感百姓，義足以結英雄，人懷其德，豪傑並用，如此，宗廟社稷宜未滅也，光武雖復賢才，大業詎可冀哉！

translations.literal: If Mang had deeply pondered Yin and Zhou's arts of taking and preserving, honoured virtue, applied himself to benevolence and righteousness, practised trustworthiness and substance, cast off flourish and falsity, spread kindness over All Under Heaven for eighteen years, so that kindness could move the hundred surnames and righteousness could bind the heroes, with every heart cherishing his virtue and stalwarts employed together—thus, the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain ought not yet to have perished; though Guangwu might again be gifted with talent, how could great enterprise have been hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Wang Mang had studied how early dynasties won and kept the throne: he might have cultivated genuine benevolence, kept his word, shed the theatrical virtue, and spent eighteen years actually feeding the realm until the people cherished him and bold men rallied. The altars might still stand; even a genius like Guangwu would have had no opening.

sentences.zh: 莽即位之後，自謂得天人之助，以為功廣三王，德茂唐、虞，乃自驕矜，奮其威詐，班宣符讖，震暴殘酷，窮凶極惡，人怨神怒，冬雷電以驚其耳目，夏地動以惕其心腹。

translations.literal: After Mang ascended the throne, he deemed himself assisted by Heaven and man, thought his merit vaster than the Three Kings and his virtue lusher than Tang or Yu, and therefore grew prideful, flaunted his might and deceit, promulgated talismanic prophecies, displayed violence and cruelty, exhausted what's most vicious and evil, so man resented and spirits raged; in winter thunder and lightning startled his ears and eyes, in summer the earth quaked to warn his heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he decided Heaven and humanity were his sponsors, bragged that he outshone the Three Kings and rivalled Yao and Shun, then turned swaggering and cruel, peddled forged omens, and ruled by terror until men and gods alike cursed him—winter lightning slapped his ears, summer tremors nagged at his gut.

sentences.zh: 而莽猶不知覺悟，方復重行不順時之令，竟連伍之刑，佞媚者親幸，忠諫者誅夷。

translations.literal: Yet Mang still knew no awakening; he just then again heavily enforced untimely ordinances, extended to the linked-five[-household] punishments, treated the sycophantic as intimate favourites, and executed and exterminated those who loyally remonstrated.
