translations.idiomatic: He still would not learn: he doubled down on senseless edicts, chained neighbours into collective guilt, promoted flatterers, and slaughtered anyone who told the truth.

sentences.zh: 由是天下忿憤，內外俱發，四海分崩，城池不守，身死於匹夫之手，為天下笑，豈不異哉！

translations.literal: From this All Under Heaven seethed with anger, inner and outer alike erupted, the four seas split and crumbled, city walls were not preserved, he died in the hands of a common fellow, and became the laughingstock of the realm—how is it not strange!
translations.idiomatic: The realm boiled over, revolt flared inside and out, and when the frontiers collapsed he died at a commoner's knife—an empire's joke. How could it be otherwise?

sentences.zh: 其所由然者，非取之過，而守之非道也。

translations.literal: What from this ensued was not excess in taking, but guarding by a way that was not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The failure was not that he had stolen the throne but that he guarded it without rectitude.

sentences.zh: 莽既屠肌，六合雲擾，劉聖公已立而不辨，盆子承之而覆敗，公孫述又稱帝於蜀漢。

translations.literal: Mang having already slaughtered down to [the people's] flesh, the six directions were roiled like clouds; Liu Shenggong was already enthroned yet could not impose order; Penzi succeeded him yet overturned in defeat; Gongsun Shu again styled himself emperor in Shu-Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang's butcheries had left the populace raw, turmoil rolled through every quarter: Liu Xuan styled himself emperor but never imposed order; Liu Penzi inherited the sham and collapsed; then Gongsun Shu declared another court in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 如此數子，固非所謂應天順人者，徒為光武之驅除者耳。

translations.literal: Such several sons, by their nature, are not what one calls answering Heaven and complying with humanity; they merely acted as Guangwu's swept-path men.
translations.idiomatic: None of those men truly answered Heaven's charge or embodied the people's will; they merely cleared Guangwu's path for him.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，蓋亦天下之天下，非一人之天下也。

translations.literal: As for All Under Heaven, in general it is likewise All Under Heaven's All Under Heaven—it is not one man's All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The realm belongs to everyone who dwells under Heaven, not to a single occupant of the throne.

sentences.zh: 「殷商之旅，其會如林，矢於牧野，維予侯興。

translations.literal: 'The hosts of Yin and Shang, their assembly like a forest; arraying at Shepherd Wild, here our noble lord mounts.'
translations.idiomatic: The ode runs: ‘The Yin-Shang legions gathered thick as timber; arrows flew at Muye—for us the march-lord sparks the charge.’

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「侯服于周，天命靡常。

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. Again it states: 'The noble ranks obey Zhou—Heaven's Mandate is not constant.'
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere it adds: ‘When vassals bow before Zhou's king, Heaven's decree shifts without fixed rule.’

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，主非常人也，有德則天下歸之，無德則天下叛之。

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. From this speaking it, the ruler is not an ordinary person: possessing virtue then All Under Heaven returns to him, lacking virtue then All Under Heaven rebels against him.
translations.idiomatic: From those verses it follows that the sovereign cannot be judged as an ordinary man: virtue draws the realm toward him; its absence pushes it away.

sentences.zh: 故古之明王，其勞心遠慮，常如臨川無津涯。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient enlightened kings worried their minds and pondered distant [matters]; constantly it was as facing a river without ford or bank.
translations.idiomatic: The wisest kings of old wore themselves down with long views, always feeling as though they stood on a riverbank with neither bridge nor opposite shore.

sentences.zh: 於是法天地，象四時，隆恩德，敬大臣，近忠直，遠佞人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they modelled Heaven and earth, patterned the four seasons, magnified gracious virtue, revered great ministers, drew near loyalty and straightforwardness, and kept distance from sycophants.
translations.idiomatic: So they took heaven and earth for their pattern and the seasons for their rhythm; they thickened kindness, honoured high ministers, kept honest advisers close and flatterers at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 仁孝著乎宮牆，弘化洽乎兆庶；

translations.literal: Benevolence and filial piety shone inside the palace walls; extensive transformation harmonised the myriad commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Filial tenderness lit the women's quarters while his moral influence steeped the myriad households;

sentences.zh: 為平直如砥矢，信義感人神。

translations.literal: [His] deportment stood straight level as grindstone arrow[-shafts]; trust and righteousness moved humans and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: his manner stayed straight as polished arrow-shafts on a whetstone, and sincerity moved both subjects and unseen powers.

sentences.zh: 雖有椒房外戚之寵，不受其委曲之言；

translations.literal: Although there existed favour for empress chambers and maternal kin, [he] did not accept their roundabout words;
translations.idiomatic: Even when imperial in-laws leaned on palace favour, he refused their roundabout pleas;

sentences.zh: 雖有近習愛幸之豎，不聽其姑息之辭。

translations.literal: although there existed close-attendant favourites of the petty sort, [he] did not heed their placating rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: even intimate eunuchs and painted favourites failed when they cooed placations.

sentences.zh: 四門穆穆，辟而不闔，待諫者而無忌。

translations.literal: The four gates were solemnly ordered, stood open yet not barred shut, awaited remonstrators without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The four gates stayed ceremoniously open—never barred against the man who came to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 恆戰戰慄栗，不忘戒懼，所以欲永終天祿，恐為將來賢 聖之驅除也。

translations.literal: Constantly trembling and shivering, not forgetting caution and dread—thereby intending forever to conclude Heaven's stipend yet fearing to become swept-path fare for sage worthies thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: They shivered awake every night lest they squander Heaven's bounty and someday play stepping-stone to worthier heirs.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞之，懼危者，常安者也；

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has heard it said: One who dreads peril is perpetually secure;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that those who dread danger usually stay upright;

sentences.zh: 憂亡者，恆存者也。

translations.literal: one who worries about perishing endures perpetual survival.
translations.idiomatic: those who rehearse catastrophe tend to endure.

sentences.zh: 使夫有國之君能安不忘危，則本枝百世，長保榮祚，名位與天地無窮，亦何慮乎為來者之驅除哉！

translations.literal: If lords possessing the state could be secure yet not forget peril, then root and branches [would flourish] hundred generations, long preserve honoured fortune, fame and standing [would be] limitless with Heaven and earth—is there then worry over becoming swept-path fare for whoever comes!
translations.idiomatic: Let any ruler clutch safety without forgetting peril, and the dynastic trunk will sprout centuries of shade, honours will hold until sky and soil wear out—and who then needs dread being another founder's prelude?

sentences.zh: 傳有之曰：「狂夫之言，明主察焉。」

translations.literal: The tradition possesses a saying: 'The madcap's speech—an enlightened ruler scrutinises it.'
translations.idiomatic: The classics insist: ‘Even reckless talk deserves a clearsighted ruler's ear.’

sentences.zh: 其二曰：士之立業，行非一概。

translations.literal: The second reads: Establishing deed for shi is not alike in conduct on a single model.
translations.idiomatic: The second strand says: gentlemen build careers along more than one moral road.

sentences.zh: 吳起貪官，母死不歸，殺妻求將，不孝之甚。

translations.literal: Wu Qi coveted office, [when] his mother died did not return, killed his wife to seek generalship—extremely unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi chased rank without burying his mother and murdered his wife for a command—monstrously unfilial.

sentences.zh: 然在魏，使秦人不敢東向；

translations.literal: Yet in Wei he caused Qin people not to dare face east;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Wei he froze Qin's armies from turning east;

sentences.zh: 在楚，則三晉不敢南謀。

translations.literal: in Chu, then the three Jins did not dare plot southward.
translations.idiomatic: in Chu he kept the three successor states from striking south.

sentences.zh: 曾參、閔騫，誠孝子也，不能宿夕離其親，豈肯出身致死，涉危險之地哉！

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and Min Qian were truly filial sons; they could not overnight leave their kin—how could they be willing to emerge body to die, wading into perilous places!
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen and Min Qian were paragons of filial piety who would not leave a parent's side for a single night—hardly the sort to charge into mortal danger abroad.

sentences.zh: 今大晉應期運之所授，齊聖美于有虞，而吳人不臣，稱帝私附，此亦國之羞也。

translations.literal: Now Great Jin has received what the ordained moment confers—the sage clarity matches Yu [-Shun's reign]—yet Wu people do not submit as ministers, privately attach and style themselves emperor; this likewise is the state's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Under Great Jin Heaven has delivered its mandate—the court's enlightenment rivals the age of Yu—yet the Wu regime still withholds tribute and enthrones itself, which remains a blot on imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲致熊羆之士，不二心之臣，使奮威淮浦、震服蠻荊者，故宜疇咨博采，廣開貢士之路，薦岩穴，舉賢才，征命考試，匪俊莫用。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to summon bear-like warriors and ministers whose hearts know no divided loyalty—such as make might flourish along the Huai shore and awe the barbarous Jing—then rightly you ought to enquire everywhere, broadly gather, widen the road presenting tribute scholars, recommend [men from] crag caves, raise worthy talent, summon by edict them to examination—and employ none who are not eminent.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to leash real fighters and steadfast ministers—the kind whose roar freezes the Yangzi marshes—you must cast the net wider: open avenues for recommended scholars, pull talent out of hillside recluses, issue summons and probationary posts, and refuse anyone who lacks distinction.

sentences.zh: 今台閣選舉，塗塞耳目，九品訪人，唯問中正。

translations.literal: Now Tower-Pavilion selections block eyes and ears, the Nine Ranks enquire into men only by asking the impartial rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Today Secretariat appointments stumble blind: the nine-grade system reduces every judgment to whatever the local rectifier whispers.

sentences.zh: 故據上品者，非公侯之子孫，則當塗之昆弟也。

translations.literal: Therefore those occupying highest rank are, if not ducal marquises' grandsons, then those in power's elder-younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: So the top slots go either to sons of old title-holders or to brothers of whoever currently pulls the strings.

sentences.zh: 二者苟然，則蓽門蓬戶之俊，安得不有陸沈者哉！

translations.literal: If the two are thus, then how should not the outstanding of brushwood-gate thatched-houses have sunken landwards!
translations.idiomatic: When blood and connection alone advance, how can brilliant men from drafty hovels avoid sinking unread?

sentences.zh: 其三曰：昔田子方養老馬，而窮士知所歸，況居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道乎！

translations.literal: The third reads: Formerly Tian Zifang maintained old horses, and indigent shi knew where to return—how much more dwelling in All Under Heaven's vast dwelling, standing in All Under Heaven's correct position, walking All Under Heaven's great road!
translations.idiomatic: The third theme: when Tian Zifang kept his worn-out horses fed, every poor scholar knew where to find shelter—how much more should a Son of Heaven, who lives in the world's broadest house, stands on its central dais, and walks its kingly path, show the same care!

sentences.zh: 昔明王聖主，無不養老。

translations.literal: Formerly enlightened kings and sagely lords none failed to nourish the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Every sage king of old honoured the elderly.

sentences.zh: 老人眾多，未必皆賢，不可悉養。

translations.literal: The aged multitude, not necessarily all worthy, cannot all be nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Gray hair multiplies faster than virtue; you cannot pension every grandfather in the empire.

sentences.zh: 故父事三老，所以明孝；

translations.literal: Therefore treating as father the three elders manifests filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ritual ‘father service’ toward the trio of elders broadcasts true filial example;

sentences.zh: 宗事五更，所以明敬。

translations.literal: ritually treating as ancestors the Five Superiors manifests reverence.
translations.idiomatic: why the ancestral-style honour paid to five senior exemplars broadcasts respect.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「吾老以及人之老，吾幼以及人之幼。

translations.literal: Mengzi stated: 'I extend honoring my elders to honoring others' elders; I extend loving my young to loving others' young.'
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said: ‘I honour my elders and carry that honour outward; I cherish my children and widen the same tenderness to theirs.’

sentences.zh: 」今天下雖定，而華山之陽無放馬之群，桃林之下未有休息之牛，故以吳人尚未臣服故也。

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. Now though All Under Heaven is settled, south of Mount Hua there are not herds releasing horses; beneath Peach Grove there are none resting oxes—thus because Wu people still have not bent in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empire is nominally quiet, nobody is pasturing peace horses south of Huashan or spelling ox teams beneath Taolin—Wu still withholds homage, and martial readiness cannot end.

sentences.zh: 夫饑者易為食，渴者易為飲，天下元元瞻望新政。

translations.literal: As for starving men easy become food, thirsty men easy become drink; All Under Heaven's common folk gaze toward the new governance.
translations.idiomatic: The famished welcome any bowl; the parched accept any cup—the common people are watching this new reign with hungry hope.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思子方之仁，念犬馬之勞，思帷蓋之報，發仁惠之詔，廣開養老之制。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty ponder Zifang's benevolence, recall the toil of dogs and horses, consider the carriage-canopy requital, issue a humane and gracious edict, and broadly open a system nourishing the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on Tian Zifang's compassion, repay the beasts of burden who served the campaigns, remember the ruler who spared an old carriage for its faithful horse, promulgate a generous decree, and widen every old-age stipend.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：法令賞罰，莫大乎信。

translations.literal: The fourth reads: As for laws, commands, rewards, and punishments, nothing is greater than trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth theme: in law, orders, rewards, and penalties, nothing outweighs keeping faith.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「人而無信，不知其可。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'A person yet lacking trustworthiness—one does not know how he may [be employed].
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs: ‘A man who cannot keep his word is not worth hiring for anything.’

sentences.zh: 」況有養人以惠，使人以義，而可以不信行之哉！

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. How much more nourishing people with bounty, employing people with righteousness—yet could one practise these without trustworthiness!
translations.idiomatic: How much more true when you feed the people with kindness and command them by duty: who will follow a lie?

sentences.zh: 臣前為西郡太守，被州所下《己未詔書》：「羌胡道遠，其但募取樂行，不樂勿強。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly was West Commandery governor, when the province transmitted down the 'Jiwei' imperial edict: 'Qiang and Hu are road-distant—only enlist those happy to go; those unhappy, do not force.'
translations.idiomatic: When I governed the western commandery a provincial copy of the Jiwei edict arrived: ‘The Qiang and Hu live far off—recruit only willing volunteers; never drag the reluctant.’

sentences.zh: 」臣被詔書，輒宣恩廣募，示以賞信，所得人名即條言征西。

translations.literal: Closing hook quotation mark. Your servant received the edict, then spread grace and recruited broadly, showed them bounty and reliability, obtained persons' names, and memorialised them item by item to General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: I announced that order, opened my purse wide, spelled out stipends honestly, rostered each volunteer, and filed the register with General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 其晉人自可差簡丁強，如法調取；

translations.literal: As for Jin people themselves they could be differentiated and selected stalwart ding[-males] by lawful regulation levies;
translations.idiomatic: Ethnic Jin households could supply conscripts through the ordinary roster;

sentences.zh: 至於羌胡，非恩意告諭，則無欲度金城、河西者也。

translations.literal: as for Qiang and Hu, without gracious intent informing and instructing them, none desired to ford Jincheng and west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: but the upland tribes would never have crossed toward Jincheng and the corridor west of the Yellow River without coaxing guarantees.

sentences.zh: 自往每興軍渡河，未曾有變，故刺史郭綏勸帥有方，深加獎厲，要許重報。

translations.literal: From-of-old whenever raising armies crossing the river not once were there disturbances; hence Governor Guo Sui persuaded the marshal with methods, profoundly added rewards and urgings, and promised weighty repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier campaigns across the river had never turned mutinous, so Governor Guo Sui managed the column with skill, heaped praise, and swore a fat reward.

sentences.zh: 是以所募感恩利賞，遂立績效，功在第一。

translations.literal: Therefore those recruited, grateful for profit and bounty, thereupon established merit and effect; merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: The recruits repaid generosity with courage, nailed the mission, and finished top of the merit list.

sentences.zh: 今州郡督將，並已受封，羌胡健兒，或王或侯，不蒙論敘也。

translations.literal: Now prefecture governors and overseer-generals have together already received investiture [rewards]; Qiang and Hu stalwarts perhaps [made] kings or marquises—yet do not receive narrative of discussion [for rewards].
translations.idiomatic: Today every provincial chief has his patent of honour, while the Qiang and Hu companies who actually won the field—some even ennobled as kings or marquises—watch their claims vanish from the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 晉文猶不貪原而失信，齊桓不惜地而背盟，況聖主乎！

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin still was not greedy for Yuan and broke trust; Duke Huan of Qi still did not spare territory and betray the covenant—how much more a sage lord!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin refused to cheat his way to Yuan, and Duke Huan of Qi refused to betray an ally for turf—surely Our Sage can outdo petty faithlessness.

sentences.zh: 其五曰：昔周、漢之興，樹親建德，周因五等之爵，漢有河山之誓。

translations.literal: The fifth reads: Formerly Zhou and Han arose, planted kin and established virtue; Zhou relied on the five-grade nobility, Han possessed the river-mountain oaths.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth theme: Zhou and Han both rose by enfeoffing kin and weaving moral obligation—Zhou through its five ranks, Han through the iron pledge carved on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，神器奪於重臣，國祚移於他人。

translations.literal: When it reached their decline, the divine regalia was wrested from weighty ministers, the state's fortune shifted to other men.
translations.idiomatic: At their fall the sacred vessels passed to overmighty servants and the dynasty's luck jumped surnames.

sentences.zh: 故滅周者秦，非姬姓也；

translations.literal: Therefore what extinguished Zhou was Qin—not the Ji surname;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ultimately fell to Qin, not to another branch of Ji;

sentences.zh: 代漢者魏，非劉氏也。

translations.literal: what replaced Han was Wei—not the Liu lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Han yielded to Wei, not to another house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 於今國家大計，使異姓無裂土專封之邑，同姓並據有連城之地，縱復令諸王後世子孫還自相並，蓋亦楚人失繁弱於雲夢，尚未為亡其弓也。

translations.literal: As for today's great state blueprint: causing different surnames to lack parcels of earth and monopoly enfeoffed townsites, causing same surname jointly to occupy cities linked like strings—supposing moreover you command various kings' posterity grandsons therein to revert to mutual annexation—probably it is likewise Chu men losing Fanruo amidst Yunmeng, still not construed as losing their bow.
translations.idiomatic: Our present design bars outsiders from walled fiefs while stacking linked citadels in princely hands; even if those same princes claw each other apart later on, it is still like the Chu huntsman losing his Fanruo bow at Yunmeng—someone else's gain, barely a scratch on Chu itself.

sentences.zh: 其於神器不移他族，則始祖不遷之廟，萬年億兆不改其名矣。

translations.literal: As for thereby the divine regalia not shifting to other lineages—then Founding Ancestor's non-shifting shrine, myriad years and trillionfold will not alter its names.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the celestial symbol from drifting to strangers, and the founder's evergreen shrine retains its honours forever unaltered.

sentences.zh: 大晉諸王二十餘人，而公侯伯子男五百餘國，欲言其國皆小乎，則漢祖之起，俱無尺土之地，況有國者哉！

translations.literal: Great Jin possesses over twenty kings, yet dukes marquises earls viscounts barons numbering over five hundred polities—wishing to declare their states all small?, then Han Ancestor's rise equally lacked even a chi of territory—how much more those possessing states!
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin divides more than twenty princes among upwards of five hundred titled baronies—were we to sniff that those plots are petty, recall that Emperor Gaozu began without a thumb's breadth of soil, while these lords already hold cities.

sentences.zh: 將謂大晉世世賢聖，而諸侯之胤常不肖邪，則放勳欽明而有丹硃，瞽瞍頑凶面虞舜。

translations.literal: Or shall we say Great Jin age after age is sagely while the feudal lords' descendants are constantly unworthy?—then Fangxun was perspicacious yet had Danzhu; Gusou was foolish and vicious yet surfaced Yu Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Neither can one pretend every future prince will be worthless while Jin stays perpetually luminous—Yao the glittering sire still fathered Danzhu, yet blind brutish Gusou spawned Shun.

sentences.zh: 天下有事無不由兵，而無故多樹兵本，廣開亂原，臣故曰五等不便也。

translations.literal: All Under Heaven has affairs none not stemming from armies; yet groundlessly many planting army roots broadly opens rebellion's origins—your servant thus states the five-grade [system] is not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Every crisis begins with armies, yet gratuitously multiplying warlord bases pours fuel on rebellion—so Your Servant urges that the Zhou-style pyramid of five ranks spells trouble.

sentences.zh: 臣以為可如前表，諸王宜大其國，增益其兵，悉遣守籓，使形勢足以相接，則陛下可高枕而臥耳。

translations.literal: Your servant judges one may enact the prior memorial: the kings ought to enlarge their polities and increase their soldiery, entirely dispatch guarding the border fiefs, enable terrain and disposition sufficient to interconnect—then Your Majesty can pillow high yet lie.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt last year's proposal: widen princely domains and their garrisons, station them firmly on the borders, tighten their fronts into a continuous shield—after that Your Majesty truly can sleep on a piled pillow.

sentences.zh: 臣以為諸侯伯子男名號皆宜改易之，使封爵之制，祿奉禮秩，並同天下諸侯之例。

translations.literal: Your servant judges the feudal lords earls viscounts barons' titles all ought be reformed and altered, causing enfeoffment's system—stipends, salaries, ritual order entirely to match All Under Heaven's various marquises' precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Strip back the dizzying tide of dukes and barons until their patents, salaries, and court ritual match those of ordinary marquises.

sentences.zh: 臣聞與覆車同軌者未嘗安也，與死人同病者未嘗生也，與亡國同法者未嘗存也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that one who shares track with an overturned cart has never been secure; one who shares illness with the dead has never lived; one who shares law with a perished state has never survived.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard: ride the same ruts as a wrecked chariot and you will not stay upright; share a corpse's symptoms and you will not draw breath; copy a dead empire's statutes and you will not endure.

sentences.zh: 況夫巍巍大晉，方將登太山，禪梁父，刻石書勳，垂示無窮。

translations.literal: How much more the towering lofty Great Jin, presently about to ascend Great Mountain, enact the Liangfu fief[-rite], carve stone documenting merit, suspend display without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Especially now, when lofty Great Jin is ready to ascend Mount Tai, perform the Liangfu thanksgiving rite, and chisel everlasting boasts into cliff stone.

sentences.zh: 宜遠鑒往代興廢，深為嚴防，使著事奮筆，必有紀焉。

translations.literal: Ought distantly mirror former dynasties' rise and ruin, deepen thereby strict guard, enabling those who wield matters and flourish brush necessarily to possess records therein.
translations.idiomatic: Look deep into former dynasties' rises and collapses and shore up every precaution, so annalists setting brush to parchment will preserve a truthful record.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹恥其君不為堯、舜，此臣所以私懷慷慨，自忘輕賤者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin was ashamed that his lord was not Yao or Shun—this is why your servant therefore privately harbours fervent zeal, forgetting himself light base.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin could not abide a mediocre king—that is why this memorial burns in me until I forget my own slight station.

sentences.zh: 灼書奏，帝覽而異焉，擢為明威將軍、魏興太守。

translations.literal: Zhuo's memorial being submitted, the Emperor perused and marvelled at it, promoted him to General Who Clarifies Might, Weixing governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zhuo's essay reached the throne, the emperor read it with wonder and raised him to General Who Clarifies Might and governor of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 閻纘，字續伯，巴西安漢人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zuan, style Xubo, was a man of Anhan in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, whose courtesy name was Xubo, came from Anhan in Baxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖圃，為張魯功曹，勸魯降魏，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: Grandfather Pu served Zhang Lu as Chief Clerk, urged Lu to surrender to Wei, and was invested Marquis of Pingle township.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan Pu rose to chief clerk under Zhang Lu, persuaded Lu to capitulate to Wei, and earned the marquisate of Pingle township.

sentences.zh: 父璞，嗣爵，仕吳至牂柯太守。

translations.literal: Father Pu inherited the fief and served Wu, reaching Administrator of Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min Pu inherited the title, served Eastern Wu, and rose to governor of Zangke.

sentences.zh: 纘僑居河南新安，少游英豪，多所交結，博覽墳典，該通物理。

translations.literal: Zuan sojourned south of the river in Henan Xin'an; in youth he roamed among heroes and made many alliances; he read widely in the classical tomes and comprehended the patterns of things.
translations.idiomatic: Min Zuan had settled south of the Yellow River in Xin'an, ran with bold company in his youth, and read his way through the canon until the world's workings made sense to him.

sentences.zh: 父卒，繼母不慈，纘恭事彌謹。

translations.literal: When father died, the stepmother was not kind; Zuan served her with reverence ever more meticulously.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died, his stepmother turned cold; he only served her with tighter courtesy.

sentences.zh: 而母疾之愈甚，乃誣纘盜父時金寶，訟於有司。

translations.literal: Yet mother hated him yet more severely; then falsely accused Zuan of stealing father's-time gold and jewels, and litigated him before the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: She grew crueler still: she invented a theft of his father's old treasures and dragged him before the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 遂被清議十餘年，纘無怨色，孝謹不怠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bore pure-reputation condemnation over ten years; Zuan showed no colour of resentment, filial-care reverence without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade the gossip of the Nine Ranks ruined him anyway; he never wore resentment on his face and never slacked as a son.

sentences.zh: 母后意解，更移中正，乃得復品。

translations.literal: Mother afterward intention resolved; further shifted Central Rectifier; then obtained restored rating.
translations.idiomatic: When she relented at last and the Central Rectifier was replaced, his rank could be restored.

sentences.zh: 為太傅楊駿舍人，轉安復令。

translations.literal: Became retainer to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, transferred to magistrate of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Yang Jun's household as a retainer, then was rotated out as magistrate of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 駿之誅也，纘棄官歸，要駿故主簿潘岳、掾崔基等共葬之。

translations.literal: At Jun's execution, Zuan abandoned office and returned, importuned Jun's former chief clerk Pan Yue, aide Cui Ji, et al., jointly to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell, Zuan resigned and went home, then pressed Yang's old chief clerk Pan Yue, aide Cui Ji, and others into giving him a decent burial.

sentences.zh: 基、嶽畏罪，推纘為主。

translations.literal: Ji, Yue feared crime; pushed Zuan to be chief.
translations.idiomatic: Cui and Pan were terrified of guilt and pushed Zuan to lead the affair.

sentences.zh: 墓成，當葬，駿從弟模告武陵王澹，將表殺造意者。

translations.literal: Tomb completed, when time to bury, Jun's cousin Mo reported to Prince Dan of Wuling, intending memorialize killing those who conceived the scheme.
translations.idiomatic: The grave was nearly ready when Yang Jun's cousin Yang Mo told Prince Dan of Wuling he would memorialize for the execution of whoever had dreamed up the burial.

sentences.zh: 眾咸懼，填塚而逃，纘獨以家財成墓，葬駿而去。

translations.literal: All alike feared, filled mound and fled; Zuan alone with family wealth completed tomb, buried Jun and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The company panicked, shoveled earth in panic, and scattered; Zuan alone spent his own fortune to finish the work, buried Yang Jun, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒鄒湛以纘才堪佐著作，薦于秘書監華嶠。

translations.literal: Libationer of the National Academy Zou Zhan deemed Zuan's talent fit assistant composition, recommended him to Librarian-in-Chief Hua Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan, libationer of the academy, thought Zuan could help compile the histories and commended him to Hua Qiao, the librarian-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「此職閑廩重，貴勢多爭之，不暇求其才。

translations.literal: Qiao said: 'This duty is idle, granary-grain heavy; noble power much contends it; no leisure to seek its talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao answered, 'That chair pays well for light work—every powerful family squabbles for it. Nobody has time to ask whether anyone there can write.'

sentences.zh: 」遂不能用。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon could not employ.
translations.idiomatic: So he never took him on.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒引為西戎校尉司馬，有功，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian drew him as marshal to the Colonel of Western Rong; had merit; enfeoffed Marquis of Pingle township.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Hejian recruited him as army marshal under the western frontier colonel; he earned merit and received the village marquisate of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子之廢也，纘輿棺詣闕，上書理太子之冤曰：

translations.literal: At Crown Prince Minhuai's deposition, Zuan bore coffin arrived at palace gate, submitted memorial sorting crown prince's wrong, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, Zuan shouldered a coffin to the palace gate and filed a memorial to clear Sima Yu's name. It read:

sentences.zh: 伏見赦文及榜下前太子遹手疏，以為驚愕。

translations.literal: Prostrate I have seen amnesty text and posted-below former crown prince Yu's own draft; I deemed it shock.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the amnesty edict and the former crown prince's plea, posted beneath it, and I am stunned.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，臣子悖逆，未有如此之甚也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, minister-son rebellions, never had like this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In all of history no subject or son's revolt has ever cut this deep.

sentences.zh: 幸賴天慈，全其首領。

translations.literal: Fortunately rely Heaven's kindness, preserve complete his head-neck.
translations.idiomatic: Only Heaven's mercy has spared his life.

sentences.zh: 臣伏念遹生於聖父而至此者，由於長養深宮，沈淪富貴，受饒先帝，父母驕之。

translations.literal: Your servant prostrate reflects: Yu born of sage father yet reached here, from being long reared deep palace, sunk in wealth-nobility, received surplus late emperor, father-mother spoiled him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes Yu was sired by a sage-king yet came to this because he was raised behind high walls, drowned in luxury, pampered by the late emperor, and indulged by his parents.

sentences.zh: 每見選師傅下至群吏，率取膏粱擊鐘鼎食之家，稀有寒門儒素如衛綰、周文、石奮、疏廣，洗馬、舍人亦無汲黯、鄭莊之比，遂使不見事父事君之道。

translations.literal: Each time I see selection from tutors down to crowd clerks, generally take fat-grain strike-bell tripod-eat households, rarely have cold-gate Confucian-plain like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, Shu Guang; tutor-in-attendance, retainer likewise have no Ji An, Zheng Zhuang comparison; thereby caused not to see serving-father serving-ruler Way.
translations.idiomatic: Look at everyone from his tutors down to clerks: they are almost always plutocrats who dine to the chime of bells. You never see poor scholars like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, or Shu Guang, nor stewards comparable to Ji An or Zheng Zhuang—so he never learned how to obey a father or a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 臣案古典，太子居以士禮，與國人齒，以此明先王欲令知先賤然後乃貴。

translations.literal: Your servant cases classical models: crown prince dwells by knight ritual, ranks with state's people—by this clarify former kings wished make him know first low afterward then noble.
translations.idiomatic: The canon says an heir should live by the rites of a knight and stand in line with commoners—precisely so a king teaches him humility before greatness.

sentences.zh: 自頃東宮亦微太盛，所以致敗也。

translations.literal: Since lately Eastern Palace likewise slightly too flourishing, that by which brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the Eastern Palace has itself swelled beyond measure—that is why it collapsed.

sentences.zh: 非但東宮，曆觀諸王師友文學，皆豪族力能得者，率非龔遂、王陽，能以道訓。

translations.literal: Not only Eastern Palace: surveying kings' tutor-friends literature, all powerful clans strength can obtain, generally not Gong Sui, Wang Yang, able by Way to instruct.
translations.idiomatic: And it is not only the heir: every prince's friends and literary advisers are bought with clan muscle. Few are another Gong Sui or Wang Yang who could teach the Way.

sentences.zh: 友無亮直三益之節，官以文學為名，實不讀書，但共鮮衣好馬，縱酒高會，嬉遊博弈，豈有切磋，能相長益！

translations.literal: Friends lack bright-straight three-benefits integrity; office by literature as name, truly not read books, only together fine clothes good horses, release wine high feasts, sport-travel chess-betting—how have polish-debate, able mutually grow benefit!
translations.idiomatic: Those 'friends' lack the stern friendship the Master praised. Offices called 'literary' never open a book; they flaunt silks and horses, throw roaring parties, dice, and hunts. Where is honest argument to sharpen character?

sentences.zh: 臣常恐公族遲陵，以此歎息。

translations.literal: Your servant constantly fears ducal clans slack-decay; by this sigh.
translations.idiomatic: I have long dreaded the wasting of the imperial house—and this is why I sigh.

sentences.zh: 今遹可以為戒，恐其被斥，棄逐遠郊，始當悔過，無所復及。

translations.literal: Now Yu may take as warning; fear his being cast-off, abandoned driven far outskirts, beginning then repent faults, nothing again reach.
translations.idiomatic: Let Yu serve as warning. If you cast him out to some border post, he may repent when nothing can be salvaged.

sentences.zh: 昔戾太子無狀，稱兵距命，而壺關三老上書，有田千秋之言，猶曰：「子弄父兵，罪應笞耳！

translations.literal: Formerly Rebel Heir misbehaved, raised arms resist mandate; yet Huguan three-old submitted memorial, had Tian Qianqiu's words, still said: 'Son played father's arms, crime should birching ear!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ju of Han still rose in arms against his father, yet the elder of Huguan reminded the throne that a son who borrows his father's army deserves only a flogging.'

sentences.zh: 」漢武感悟之，築思子之台。

translations.literal: Han Wu took it to heart, built Thinking-Son terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu listened and raised the Terrace for the Longing Son.

sentences.zh: 今遹無狀，言語悖逆，受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕于戾太子，尚可禁持，重選保傅。

translations.literal: Now Yu misbehaves, speech rebellious; receiving crime days, dare not lose Way; still lighter than Rebel Heir, still can restrain-hold, heavily reselect guardian-tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Yu has misbehaved and his language was treasonous, yet when sentence came he kept his bearing—still a lighter case than Prince Ju. He can be held in check if you choose new guardians and tutors with care.

sentences.zh: 如司空張華，道德深遠，乃心忠誠，以為之師。

translations.literal: Such as Minister of Works Zhang Hua, virtue-morality deep far, heart loyal-sincere—take him as tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Hua has profound virtue and a loyal heart—name him senior tutor.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉寔，寒苦自立，終始不衰，年同呂望，經藉不廢，以為之保。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Liu Shi, cold-bitter self-stood, end-beginning not decline, age same Lü Wang, classics not abandoned—take him as guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Liu Shi rose from hardship without bowing; he matches Lü Wang in years and never sets the classics aside—name him guardian.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射裴頠，明允恭肅，體道居正，以為之友。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Masters of Writing Pei Wei, bright-trustworthy reverent-stern, embody Way dwell correct—take him as friend.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Pei Wei is lucid, honest, and grave, and he walks the straight path—name him companion-adviser.

sentences.zh: 置游談文學，皆選寒門孤宦以學行自立者，及取服勤更事、涉履艱難、事君事親、名行素聞者，使與共處。

translations.literal: Set wandering-talk literature, all select cold-gate orphan-office those by learning-conduct self-stood, and take wear-diligence change-affairs, tread-travel hardship-danger, serve-ruler serve-kin, name-conduct plain-heard, make with them dwell together.
translations.idiomatic: Fill the 'literary' slots with poor-born officials who live by scholarship, and add men hardened by real service—men known for serving ruler and family through trouble—and let them room with him.

sentences.zh: 使嚴御史監護其家，絕貴戚子弟、輕薄賓客。

translations.literal: Make stern censor supervise-guard his house, cut off noble-kin sons-young, frivolous guests.
translations.idiomatic: Put a strict censor over his household and shut out noble boys and flashy guests.

sentences.zh: 如此，左右前後，莫非正人。

translations.literal: Like this left-right front-rear, none not correct men.
translations.idiomatic: Then whoever stands near him morning and night will be upright.

sentences.zh: 師傅文學，可令十日一講，使共論議於前。

translations.literal: Tutor-guardian literature, can order tenth-day one lecture, make together debate discourse before.
translations.idiomatic: Have tutors and literary officers lecture once every ten days and argue policy in front of him.

sentences.zh: 敕使但道古今孝子慈親，忠臣事君，及思愆改過之義，皆聞善道，庶幾可全。

translations.literal: Ordered agents only discourse ancient-modern filial sons kind-parents, loyal ministers serve ruler, and think-fault mend-pass meaning—all hear good Way, perhaps nearly can preserve whole.
translations.idiomatic: Tell them to speak only of filial sons, faithful ministers, and how to reckon with sin and mend it—pour good counsel into his ears until something takes root.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲有罪，放之三年，思庸克復，為殷明王。

translations.literal: Formerly Tai Jia had crime, banished three years, thought ordinary able restore, became Yin enlightened king.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia offended his ministers and spent three years in exile pondering duty; when he returned he became a worthy king of Shang.

sentences.zh: 又魏文帝懼於見廢，夙夜自祗，竟能自全。

translations.literal: Further Wei Emperor Wen feared at seeing abolish; early-night self-watchful; in end able self-preserve-complete.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei lived in dread of deposition, disciplined himself night and day, and survived.

sentences.zh: 及至明帝，因母得罪，廢為平原侯，為置家臣庶子，師友文學，皆取正人，共相匡矯。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Ming—because mother got crime—demoted Plains Marquis—set retainers heir-trainees, tutor-friends literature, all taken correct men, together mutually rectify-straight.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei was stripped to marquis of the plain when his mother fell; handlers gave him steward, tutors, companions, and literary aides—all upright men—to steady one another.

sentences.zh: 兢兢慎罰，事父以孝，父沒，事母以謹，聞于天下，於今稱之。

translations.literal: Fearful-fearful careful punishment; serve father with filial; father deceased, serve mother with care; heard throughout Under Heaven—unto today praises him.
translations.idiomatic: He threaded every danger with caution, honoured his father in life and nursed his mother after—stories everyone still repeats.

sentences.zh: 漢高皇帝數置酒於庭，欲廢太子，後四皓為師，子房為傅，竟復成就。

translations.literal: Han High Emperor repeatedly set ale in courtyard, wished abolish crown prince; afterward Four Hoary became tutors, Zifang became guardian—in end again accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu kept toasting himself toward deposing Liu Ying until the Four Hoary Heads arrived as tutors and Zhang Liang as guardian—then the succession held.

sentences.zh: 前事不忘，後事之戒。

translations.literal: Before affairs not forgetting, after affairs' warning.
translations.idiomatic: Remember the past if you would govern the future.

sentences.zh: 孟軻有雲，「孤臣孽子，其操心也危，慮患也深」，故多善功。

translations.literal: Meng Ke has saying: 'Orphan minister sinful son, their exercise care also peril, ponder trouble also deep'—therefore much good accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said that a minister out in the cold and a son born in disgrace 'live on a knife's edge and think hard about peril'—and that is why they often accomplish good.

sentences.zh: 李斯云：「慈母多敗子，嚴家無格虜。

translations.literal: Li Si said: 'Kind mother many ruins sons; strict house no shackled captives.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si wrote, 'Too gentle a mother ruins her boys; in a stern household nobody ends in chains.'

sentences.zh: 」由陛下驕遹使至於此，庶其受罪以來，足自思改。

translations.literal: ' From Your Majesty spoiled Yu causing reach here; perhaps his receiving crime since then, enough self think reform.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spoiled Yu into this mess; perhaps suffering for it has taught him enough to change.

sentences.zh: 方今天下多虞，四夷未寧，將伺國隙。

translations.literal: Square now Under Heaven many troubles, four barbarians not quiet, generals spy state's crack.
translations.idiomatic: The realm rustles with trouble, the frontier is restless, and enemies watch for any crack in the wall.

sentences.zh: 儲副大事，不宜空虛。

translations.literal: Heir-support great matter, not appropriate empty void.
translations.idiomatic: The succession is too vital to leave hollow.

sentences.zh: 宜為大計，小復停留。

translations.literal: Ought act great plan, small again pause-stay.
translations.idiomatic: Plot for the long term and pause before you act.

sentences.zh: 先加嚴誨。

translations.literal: First add stern instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Begin with harsh instruction.

sentences.zh: 依平原侯故事，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。

translations.literal: Follow Plains Marquis precedent; if not repent-reform, abandon not yet late also.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Emperor Ming's plain-marquis model; if Yu will not mend his ways, you may still cast him off later.

sentences.zh: 臣素寒門，無力仕宦，不經東宮，情不私遹。

translations.literal: Your servant plain cold-gate, no strength office-career, not passed Eastern Palace, feeling not private to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: I am a nobody from a cold gate with no pull at court; I never served the Eastern Palace. I do not plead for Yu out of private fondness.

sentences.zh: 念昔楚國處女諫其王曰「有龍無尾」，言年四十，未有太子。

translations.literal: I recall Chu state's virgin admonished her king saying 'Has dragon no tail'—speech year forty, not yet had crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: I remember the Chu girl who warned her king he was 'a dragon without a tail'—past forty with no heir.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗備近職，雖未得自結天日，情同閽寺，悾悾之誠，皆為國計。

translations.literal: Your servant once filled near post; although not obtained self-knot Heaven sun, feeling same gate-guard, earnest-earnest sincerity, all for state's plan.
translations.idiomatic: I once held a post close to the throne; though I never won a private audience, my heart is as exposed as a gatekeeper's—every word is for the dynastic plan.

sentences.zh: 臣老母見臣為表，乃為臣卜卦，云「書禦即死」。

translations.literal: Your servant old mother seeing servant make memorial, then for servant divined hexagram, saying 'Writing reaches throne then death.'
translations.idiomatic: When my mother saw this draft she cast the yarrow for me: 'If the memorial reaches the throne, you die.'

sentences.zh: 妻子守臣，涕泣見止。

translations.literal: Wife children detained servant, weeping-tears seeing stop.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and children clung to me, weeping, begging me to stop.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為頻見拔擢，嘗為近職，此恩難忘，何以報德？

translations.literal: Your servant alone thought repeatedly seeing pull-promote, once was near post—this grace hard forget; how repay virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have been raised from nothing and once stood near the radiance of the throne; that grace is not forgotten. How else could I repay it?

sentences.zh: 唯當陳誠，以死獻忠。

translations.literal: Only ought state sincerity, by death offer loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I can only speak my mind and offer loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 輒具棺絮，伏須刑誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon prepared coffin padding, prostrate await execution-punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I have coffin and shroud ready and await the executioner's stroke.

sentences.zh: 書禦不省。

translations.literal: Memorial reached throne not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne and went unread.

sentences.zh: 及張華遇害，賈謐被誅，朝野震悚，纘獨撫華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也夫！

translations.literal: Reaching Zhang Hua meet harm, Jia Mi meet execution, court wild quaked; Zuan alone stroked Hua corpse wailed, saying: 'Early told you yield post but not willing—now fruit not avoid—fate, ah!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua was killed and Jia Mi cut down, the capital shook; Zuan alone cradled Zhang Hua's body and wept, 'I told you to yield your post and you refused—now see what fate costs.'

sentences.zh: 」過叱賈謐屍曰：「小兒亂國之由，誅其晚矣！」

translations.literal: Passing rebuked Jia Mi corpse, saying: 'Little boy disorder state's from—execute him late indeed!'
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jia Mi's corpse he spat, 'You child—this is why the realm burned. They should have killed you sooner.'

sentences.zh: 皇太孫立，纘復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Imperial great-grandson established, Zuan again submitted rough memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial great-grandson was named heir, Zuan filed another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣前上書訟太子之枉，不見省覽。

translations.literal: Your servant before submitted memorial litigate crown prince's wrong, not seen examine-view.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once petitioned for the crown prince's innocence; it was never read.

sentences.zh: 昔壺關三老陳衛太子之冤，而漢武築思子之台。

translations.literal: Formerly Huguan three-old stated Guard crown prince's wrong, yet Han Wu built Thinking-Son terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The elder of Huguan pleaded for Prince Ju, and Emperor Wu answered by building the Terrace for the Longing Son.

sentences.zh: 高廟令田千秋上書，不敢正言，托以鬼神之教，而孝武大感，月中三遷，位至丞相，乘車入殿，號曰車氏。

translations.literal: High Temple director Tian Qianqiu submitted memorial, dared not straight-speak, entrusted with ghosts-spirits teaching—yet Emperor Wu greatly moved, within month thrice promoted, rank reached chancellor, rode carriage entered hall, titled Cart clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qianqiu, caretaker of Gaozu's shrine, dared not speak plainly and framed his plea as a ghost's warning—yet Emperor Wu was so moved that within a month he promoted him three times to chancellor, let him ride a carriage into the hall, and nicknamed his line the House of the Cart.

sentences.zh: 恨臣精誠微薄，不能有感，竟使太子流離，沒命許昌。

translations.literal: Hate your servant essence-sincerity thin slight, not able have move—end caused crown prince drift-separate, lose life Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: I blame my own thin eloquence: I could not move you, and the heir wandered to his death in Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 向令陛下即納臣言，不致此禍。

translations.literal: Had ordered Your Majesty immediately accept servant words, not reach this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Had you taken my words when I first offered them, this disaster would never have come.

sentences.zh: 天贊聖意，三公獻謀，庶人賜死，罪人斯得，太子以明，臣恨其晚，無所復及。

translations.literal: Heaven assist sage intent, Three Dukes offer stratagem, commoner ordered die, criminal this obtained, crown prince thereby cleared—your servant hates its lateness, nothing again reach.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shifted your heart, the Three Dukes plotted, the culprit was ordered to die, the crime was proved, and the crown prince's name was cleared—I mourn only that justice came too late to save him.

sentences.zh: 詔書慈悼，迎喪反葬，復其禮秩，誠副眾望，不意呂、霍之變復生於今日！

translations.literal: Edict book kind-mourn, welcome bier return bury, restore his ritual-rank—truly matched crowd hope; not expected Lü, Huo change again born at today!
translations.idiomatic: Your merciful edict welcomed his bier home, restored his rites, and matched what the people wanted—who imagined we would see another Lü or Huo drama in our own day?

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書建立太孫，斯誠陛下上順先典以安社稷，中慰慈悼冤魂之痛，下令萬國心有所系。

translations.literal: Prostrate see edict establish imperial great-grandson—this truly Your Majesty above follow former canons to calm altars-and-grain, within console kind-mourn wronged souls' pain, below order myriad regions heart have what fastens.
translations.idiomatic: I see you have proclaimed the great-grandson heir: above, you heed the old pattern and steady the temples; within, you comfort wronged ghosts; below, you give the realm something to cling to.

sentences.zh: 追惟庶人，所為無狀，幾傾宗廟，賴相國、太宰至忠憤發，潛謀俱斷，奉贊聖意，以成神武。

translations.literal: Tracing recall commoner-status culprit, deeds without shape, nearly toppled ancestral temple—relied minister-in-chief, grand tutor utmost loyalty rage-rose, covert plots altogether cut, uphold assist sage intent, thereby complete divine martialness.
translations.idiomatic: Remember the stripped conspirators whose crimes nearly overturned the altars—it took the chief minister's and grand tutor's fierce loyalty and their secret strikes, all in accord with your will, to finish the coup as cleanly as a god of war.

sentences.zh: 雖周誅二叔，漢掃諸呂，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Although Zhou executed two uncles, Han swept all Lüs—not enough thereby compare.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Zhou executions of Guan and Cai and Han's massacre of the Lü clan fade beside this righteousness.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下因此大更厘改，以為永制。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty thereby great further thorough reform—take as lasting regulation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ride this tide into sweeping reform—write it as permanent statute.

sentences.zh: 禮置太子，居以士禮，與國人齒，為置官屬，皆如朋友，不為純臣。

translations.literal: Ritually install crown prince, dwell by knight ritual, rank with state's people, set official retinue, all like friends, not pure subjects.
translations.idiomatic: By classical rites the heir should live as a knight among the people; his staff should be friends, not mere vassals.

sentences.zh: 既使上厭至望，以崇孝道，又令不相嚴憚，易相規正。

translations.literal: Already make above satisfy utmost hope, thereby exalt filial Way; further order not mutually stern-fear, easy mutually regulate-correct.
translations.idiomatic: That satisfies the court's loftiest hopes and crowns filial duty, yet keeps tutor and pupil from freezing in fear so they can correct one another openly.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武既信奸讒，危害太子，復用望氣之言，欲盡誅詔獄中囚。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wu already trusted wicked slander, endangered crown prince; again used qi-watching words, wished exhaust execute edict-prison inmates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han listened to poison and ruined his heir, then listened to geomancy and meant to butcher every prisoner named in an edict.

sentences.zh: 邴吉以皇孫在焉，閉門距命，後遂擁護皇孫，督罰乳母，卒至成人，立為孝宣皇帝。

translations.literal: Bing Ji because imperial grandson was there, closed gate resisted mandate; afterward then embraced-guarded imperial grandson, supervised-punish wet-nurse, end reached adult person, established Filial Manifest emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji barred the gate because the imperial grandson was inside, then shielded the boy, disciplined the wet-nurse, and raised him to the throne as Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 苟志於忠，無往不可。

translations.literal: If resolve at loyalty, nowhere not go-able.
translations.idiomatic: Where loyalty is the aim, no road is barred.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古人雖不避死，亦由世教寬以成節。

translations.literal: Survey-view ancients—although not avoid death—also from generation teaching lenient thereby complete integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did not shun death, but their age still forgave enough of it to let integrity stand.

sentences.zh: 吉雖距詔書，事在於忠，故宥而不責。

translations.literal: Ji although resisted edict document, affair lay in loyalty—therefore pardon without blame.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji defied an edict for loyalty's sake—so he was spared and never charged.

sentences.zh: 自晉興已來，用法太嚴，遲速之間，輒加誅斬。

translations.literal: Self Jin rise since, use law too severe; delay-haste between, then add execute behead.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin arose the code has swung toward cruelty: hesitate a moment or move too fast and the headsman appears.

sentences.zh: 一身伏法，猶可強為，今世之誅，動輒滅門。

translations.literal: One body submit law, still can force-done; present age's executions, move then exterminate gate.
translations.idiomatic: A man may force himself through a solo execution, but nowadays a sentence means an exterminated lineage.

sentences.zh: 昔呂後臨朝，肆意無道。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Lü faced court, wanton conduct no Way.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü held court and indulged every cruelty.

sentences.zh: 周昌相趙，三召其王而昌不遣，先征昌入，乃後召王。

translations.literal: Zhou Chang chancellor-ed Zhao—thrice summoned its king yet Chang not dispatch—first summoned Chang enter, afterward then summoned king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang governed Zhao for the throne: three summonses for the king, and Zhou Chang refused each time until the court called Zhou Chang in first—only then could they summon the king.

sentences.zh: 此由漢制本寬，得使為快。

translations.literal: This from Han system root lenient, obtain make it swift.
translations.idiomatic: Han law was loose enough to allow that boldness.

sentences.zh: 假令如今，呂後必謂昌已反，夷其三族，則誰敢復為殺身成義者哉！

translations.literal: Suppose order like today—Empress Lü must say Chang already rebelled, level his three clans—then who again dares act die-for-righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Under our code Empress Lü would call it revolt, flatten three clans, and no one would ever die for principle again.

sentences.zh: 此法宜改，可使經遠。

translations.literal: This law ought reform, can make endure far.
translations.idiomatic: Change that law if you want the dynasty to last.

sentences.zh: 又漢初廢趙王張敖，其臣貫高謀弑高祖，高祖不誅，以明臣道。

translations.literal: Further Han beginning removed Zhao King Zhang Ao; his subject Guan Gao plotted kill Emperor Gao; Emperor Gao not execute—thereby clarify minister Way.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han deposed King Zhang Ao of Zhao when his retainer Guan Gao tried to murder Gaozu; Gaozu spared the king to teach what true vassalage means.

sentences.zh: 田叔、孟舒十人為奴，髡鉗隨王，隱親侍養，故令平安。

translations.literal: Tian Shu, Meng Shu ten men became slaves, shave-collar followed king, conceal-kin serve nurture—therefore order peace-safe.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shu, Meng Shu, and eight others shaved their heads, wore the neck-iron, and followed their lord as slaves to hide and serve him—so he lived.

sentences.zh: 向使晉法得容為義，東宮之臣得如周昌，固護太子得如邴吉，距詔不坐，伏死諫爭，則聖意必變，太子以安。

translations.literal: Had ordered Jin law obtain contain act righteousness, Eastern Palace ministers obtain like Zhou Chang, firm-guard crown prince obtain like Bing Ji, resist edict not sit crime, prostrate die remonstrate contend—then sage intent must change, crown prince thereby safe.
translations.idiomatic: Had our statutes blessed such loyalty—had Eastern Palace aides been another Zhou Chang, guardians another Bing Ji, free to defy forged orders and die remonstrating—the throne would have turned and the heir would stand today.

sentences.zh: 如田叔、孟舒侍從不罪者，則隱親左右，奸凶毒藥無緣得設，太子不夭也。

translations.literal: Like Tian Shu, Meng Shu attend-follow not crime—then conceal-kin left-right, treacherous-villain poison medicine no fate obtain set—crown prince not die young.
translations.idiomatic: If men like Tian Shu and Meng Shu could attend a disgraced prince without guilt, trusted hands would stay at his side and poisoners would find no seam—no early death for the heir.

sentences.zh: 臣每責東宮臣故無侍從者，後聞頗有于道路望車拜辭，而有司收付洛陽獄，奏科其罪。

translations.literal: Your servant each blamed Eastern Palace ministers formerly no attend-followers—but afterward heard considerably have at road-watch carriage bow farewell—yet offices seize deliver Luoyang prison, memorialize sentence their crime.
translations.idiomatic: I condemned the Eastern Palace staff for leaving no companions—then learned many bowed farewell along the roadside and were shackled into Luoyang jail on memorialized charges.

sentences.zh: 然臣故莫從，良有以也。

translations.literal: Yet servant's fellows none followed—indeed had reason thereof.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder none of his old friends dared walk with him.

sentences.zh: 又本置三率，盛其兵馬，所以宿衛防虞。

translations.literal: Further root-set three lieutenants, flourish their infantry-cavalry—thereby night-guard defence watch.
translations.idiomatic: You stationed the three Household guards and swollen their horses and spears precisely to ward the palace overnight.

sentences.zh: 而使者卒至，莫有警嚴覆請審者，此由恐畏滅族。

translations.literal: Yet agents abrupt arrive, none had alert strict double-request examine—this from dread fear extinction clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when couriers crashed the gates nobody armed the watch or demanded proof—terror of clan extinction did that.

sentences.zh: 今皇孫沖幼，去事多故。

translations.literal: Now imperial grandson tender-young, gone affairs many therefore.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson is a child in a season of fresh disasters.

sentences.zh: 若有不虞，強臣專制，奸邪矯詐，雖有相國保訓東宮，擁佑之恩同于邴吉，適可使玉體安全，宜開來防，可著於令：自今已後，諸有廢興倉卒，群臣皆得輒嚴，須錄詣殿前，面受口詔，然後為信，得同周昌不遣王節，下聽臣子隱親，得如田叔、孟舒，不加罪責，則永固儲副，以後安嗣之遠慮也。

translations.literal: If have un-foreseen—strong minister monopolize rule, treacherous-evil fake edict—although have minister-in-chief guard-instruct Eastern Palace, embrace-shield grace same as Bing Ji—only can make jade body peace-safe—ought open come safeguard, can write in statute: from now after, all have abolish-enthronement haste, crowd ministers all obtain then strict-arm, must record bring hall front, face receive mouth edict, afterward count trust—obtain match Zhou Chang not dispatch king tally; below listen subject-son conceal-kin gain like Tian Shu, Meng Shu, not add crime blame—then forever firm heir-support, thereafter secure succession far plan.
translations.idiomatic: If crisis comes—a strongman's junta, forged edicts—even a Bing Ji at the Eastern Palace saves only flesh. Open permanent safeguards: decree that sudden depositions force every minister to lock the precincts until registers reach the stair and edicts are heard mouth-to-ear; match Zhou Chang's refusal to surrender the tally; forgive hidden service like Tian Shu and Meng Shu. Then the heir survives and the lineage endures beyond our sight.

sentences.zh: 來事難知，往事可改。

translations.literal: Come affairs hard know; gone affairs can reform.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow is unknowable—yesterday can still be mended.

sentences.zh: 臣前每見詹事裴權用心懇惻，舍人秦戢數上疏啟諫；

translations.literal: Your servant formerly repeatedly saw Household Superintendent Pei Quan apply mind earnest-sincere; Gentleman-in-Attendance Qin Ji several times ascended memorial-openings remonstrating;
translations.idiomatic: I have often watched Crown Prince Household Superintendent Pei Quan serve with wrenching earnestness and Gentleman Qin Ji memorial after memorial beseech the throne.

sentences.zh: 而爰倩贈以九列，權有忠意，獨不蒙賞。

translations.literal: yet Yuan Qian posthumously gifted with Nine Columns; Quan had loyal intent, alone did not receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan Qian won posthumous honours among the Nine Ministers while Pei Quan, though loyal as any of them, received nothing.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依倩為比，以寵其魂。

translations.literal: say ought accord Qian as precedent, thereby grace his shade.
translations.idiomatic: Treat Pei Quan by the same measure granted Yuan Qian and let his ghost know favour.

sentences.zh: 推尋表疏，如秦戢輩及司隸所奏，諸敢拜辭于道路者，明詔稱揚，使微異於眾，以勸為善，以獎將來也。

translations.literal: Tracing-search memorial-tablets—such as Qin Ji's sort and Metropolitan Shepherd memorialized—all those daring bow resign along roads—bright edict praised-displayed them, causing faint difference from masses—thereby encourage doing good—thereby reward future also.
translations.idiomatic: Survey the petitions—Qin Ji's and the Metropolitan Shepherd's—praising men who dared surrender their seals in the highroad dust; your luminous edict singled them out so virtue would spread and posterity take heart.

sentences.zh: 今相國雖已保傅東宮，保其安危。

translations.literal: Now Chancellor of State although already Tutor-Protector Eastern Palace, safeguards its peace-peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State is already grand and junior tutor—he guards the heir's life and death.

sentences.zh: 至於旦夕訓誨，輔導出入，動靜劬勞，宜選寒苦之士，忠貞清正，老而不衰，如城門校尉梁柳、白衣南安硃沖比者，以為師傅。

translations.literal: Reaching dawn-evening instruction-lecture, assistant-guide exit-enter, movement-still toil-labour—ought select cold-bitter knights, loyal pure upright, old yet not failing—such as Gates Colonel Liang Liu, white-clothes Nan'an Zhu Chong's like—thereby make Tutor-Protector.
translations.idiomatic: For the daily coaching, the comings and goings, the bone-wearying round of duty, pick men of chilly gates and proven honor—men like Gates Colonel Liang Liu or the hemp-robed recluse Zhu Chong of Nan'an—and set them over him as tutors.

sentences.zh: 其侍臣以下文武將吏，且勿復取盛戚豪門子弟，若吳太妃家室及賈、郭之黨。

translations.literal: Those serving ministers below civil-martial generals clerks—forthwith again not take flourishing-kins great-gate sons-younger—such as Consort Wu's house-relations and Jia, Guo factions.
translations.idiomatic: Do not staff his attendants and guards from the riot of princely in-laws—no more of Consort Wu's clan or the Jia and Guo packs.

sentences.zh: 如此之輩，生而富溢，無念修己，率多輕薄浮華，相驅放縱，皆非所補益於吾少主者也。

translations.literal: Such ilk—born then wealth-overflow; no thought cultivate self; norm many light-thin float-flower; mutually urge unrestraint—all not that which benefits our young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Men soaked in gold from the cradle never trouble to temper themselves; they glide through life on perfume and dare—none of them strengthens a boy who must wear the crown.

sentences.zh: 皆可擇寒門篤行、學問素士、更履險易、節義足稱者，以備群臣，可輕其禮儀，使與古同，於相切磋為益。

translations.literal: All can select cold-gate pure-conduct, learning question plain knights, repeated walked peril-easy, integrity righteousness sufficient praised—thereby equip crowd ministers—can lighten their ritual-etiquette—cause with antiquity same—thereby mutually polish-cut as benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fill the household instead with poor gate scholars of tested fiber, men who have ridden fortune's switchbacks and earned a name for constancy; relax the court drill so they may speak as elders did and sharpen one another like whetstones.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝之在東宮，徐幹、劉楨為友，文學相接之道並如氣類。

translations.literal: Anciently Wei Wendi in Eastern Palace—Xu Gan, Liu Zhen as friends—literary learning connect-receive Way together like breath-kind.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei was heir, Xu Gan and Liu Zhen were his companions; their brush and book traffic breathed the same air as his own.

sentences.zh: 吳太子登，顧譚為友，諸葛恪為賓，臥同床帳，行則參乘，交如布衣，相呼以字，此則近代之明比也。

translations.literal: Wu Heir Deng—Gu Tan as friend, Zhuge Ke as guest—slept same bed-curtain, walking then three-horse chariot—association like plain cloth—mutual call by style—this then near-generation bright parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Deng of Wu kept Gu Tan as friend and Zhuge Ke as mentor; they shared a couch, rode the second chariot at his side, called one another by courtesy name like village neighbors—a mirror for our own age.

sentences.zh: 天子之子不患不富貴，不患人不敬畏，患於驕盈，不聞其過，不知稼穡之艱難耳。

translations.literal: Son-of-Heaven's sons not worry not wealth-noble; not worry people not fear-revere—worry lies in pride-overflow, not hear one's fault, not know grain-agriculture's hardship difficulty ear.
translations.idiomatic: A Son of Heaven's boy need not fear poverty or want of awe; he must dread arrogance, deafness to blame, and ignorance of what the plough costs.

sentences.zh: 至於甚者，乃不知名六畜，可不勉哉！

translations.literal: Reaching extreme ones—then not know names six domestic beasts—can not strive!
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all are heirs who cannot tell ox from horse—can we afford not to drill them?

sentences.zh: 昔周公親撻伯禽，曹參笞窋二百，聖考慈父皆不傷恩。

translations.literal: Anciently Duke Zhou personally whipped Bo Qin; Cao Can bamboo-thrashed Jiao two hundred—sagely fathers kind fathers all not harmed grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou flogged Bo Qin; Cao Can caned his son Cao Jiao two hundred strokes—holy fathers broke skin without breaking love.

sentences.zh: 今不忍小相維持，令至闕失頓相罪責，不亦誤哉！

translations.literal: Now not bear small mutual indulgent-sustain—order reach fault-miss suddenly mutually blame-punish—not also error!
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot bear a tutor's small discipline now, you will only watch the boy fail and flay his keepers later—what folly is that?

sentences.zh: 在禮太子朝夕視膳，昏定晨省，跪問安否，於情得盡。

translations.literal: Within rites crown prince dawn-dusk inspects meals—dusk-fix dawn-inquire—kneel ask peace-fouling—at feeling obtains exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual sets the heir beside his father's tray morning and night, evening his rest and dawn his health, kneeling to ask after him until duty is spent.

sentences.zh: 五日一朝，于敬既簡，於恩亦疏，易致構間。

translations.literal: Five-days one court-audience—in respect already simple; in grace also distant—easy bring about frame-between.
translations.idiomatic: An audience every five days slights filial punctilio and thins affection—an open door for slander between you.

sentences.zh: 故曰「一朝不朝，其間容刀」。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, 'If one morning he does not attend, a knife can slip into the gap.'
translations.idiomatic: The adage runs, 'Miss a single morning audience and a blade can slide into the breach.'

sentences.zh: 五日之制，起漢高祖，身為天子，父為庶人，萬機事多，故闕私敬耳。

translations.literal: Five-days regulation—rose Han Gaozu—himself was Son of Heaven—father was commoner—myriad pivot affairs many—therefore lacked private reverence ear.
translations.idiomatic: The five-day rule began with Han Gaozu, Son of Heaven whose father was still a common busyman and whose desk overflowed—so private courtesy gave way.

sentences.zh: 今主上臨朝，太子無事，專主孝養，宜改此俗。

translations.literal: Now Sovereign above holds court—crown prince without affairs—solely oversees filial nurture—ought alter this vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Today the emperor governs alone while the heir has no war to fight; nothing should stop him honoring a father daily—discard that Han habit.

sentences.zh: 《文王世子》篇曰：「王季一飯亦一飯，再飯亦再飯。

translations.literal: The chapter 'Royal Heir of King Wen' says: 'When Wang Ji took one meal he took one meal; when he took two meals he took two meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Ritual recall King Wen's heir: Wang Ji lifted his bowl once and the prince matched him; Wang Ji lifted it twice and the prince matched again.

sentences.zh: 」安有逸豫五日一覲哉！

translations.literal: ' Where is there ease-five-days-one-audience!
translations.idiomatic: Who under heaven excuses lounging toward a father's kitchen with audiences only every fifth dawn?
